        "text": "RE-call's DB-backed suite produces failures that have nothing to do with the code under test,\nrepeatedly and at wildly different scales: 15 failed + 5 errors, 473 errors, 41 failed + 59\nerrors, 8 failed + 12 errors, and single one-off errors. The manual `docker\nrun` recipe below is now `scripts/session-db.sh`:",

        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f **The exception, and only this one: a single DB-free FILE.** 2026-08-15 a reachable but\nschema-incompatible database made `conftest.py`'s session-scoped autouse\n`_bootstrap_default_test_schema` raise out of `apply_migrations`, which **ERRORed every test in the\nrepo**, including files that touch no database.     "query": "why does the test suite have no default database DSN",
    "decision": "answer",

    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "db6f1a502896606f032ba034bd0c8a9b4a0593c566efcc09156d92d5104e80a1",
        "text": "RE-call's DB-backed suite produces failures that have nothing to do with the code under test,\nrepeatedly and at wildly different scales: 15 failed + 5 errors, 473 errors, 41 failed + 59\nerrors, 8 failed + 12 errors, and single one-off errors. Every one passed on isolated re-run.\nBudget for it: the full suite is 15-20 minutes, so a false red is expensive to chase.\n\n## 2026-08-15: the root cause is fixed in the repo. Use the scripts.\n\n`tests/conftest.py` no longer defaults to `localhost:5432`. Unset, `TEST_DSN` points at port 1,\nso an unconfigured run skips loudly instead of silently sharing a database. The manual `docker\nrun` recipe below is now `scripts/session-db.sh`:",
        "source": "recall/concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.805387+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5627881623976337,
        "confidence": 0.9046980291750979,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "24cf920cc2704acd44d739e1d0fdacfb4911ab4967287ff0e7dc2fd6239a972e",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f **The exception, and only this one: a single DB-free FILE.** 2026-08-15 a reachable but\nschema-incompatible database made `conftest.py`'s session-scoped autouse\n`_bootstrap_default_test_schema` raise out of `apply_migrations`, which **ERRORed every test in the\nrepo**, including files that touch no database. An untouched file errored identically, which is how\nI knew it was not my change. `_db_available()` only skips the bootstrap when the DSN is\n*unreachable*, so the fix was to make it unreachable:\n\nRECALL_TEST_DSN=\"postgresql://nobody:nobody@127.0.0.1:1/none\" python -m pytest tests/<one_file>.py -q",
        "source": "recall/concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",
        "ordinal": 8,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.811393+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.562715470790867,
        "confidence": 0.9044354704503783,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "98a2fd0ce14fd81715161654a24b0c29caca9c76c988e34eb5209a626d3d89a3",
        "text": "Con un DB usa-e-getta (`recall_pytest`, owner `recall_beam`, pgvector 0.8.2): **1429 passed,\n1 failed, 4 skipped**. Runner riusabile: `/opt/recall-fb/run_db_tests.py` \u2014 legge il DSN da\n`/opt/recall-beam/.env`, sostituisce **solo** il nome del DB, blocca `recall_bench`/\n`sentiment_agent`/`postgres`, toglie `RECALL_DSN`, non mette mai la password su una command\nline. \u26a0\ufe0f la suite stessa rifiuta di partire se `RECALL_TEST_DSN == RECALL_DSN` (\u00abthese tests\nDROP TABLES\u00bb).",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference-recall-checkouts-vps2-pinned-2026-07-29.md",
        "ordinal": 11,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:06:22.671367+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5359236321403771,
        "confidence": 0.7551945907327549,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "83e62ed61daead12e9e9a1ddf9f7e764db0537dd0e4819d94db8d36dcd1594e0",
        "text": "\u26d4 **Never \"isolate\" a DB-free change by pointing the DSN at a dead port.** `_db_available()`\ncovers most of the suite but not all: three `tests/test_bench_systems.py::test_recall_system_*`\ntests FAIL with `psycopg.errors.ConnectionTimeout` instead of skipping, manufacturing a red that\nlooks like your change.",
        "source": "recall/concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",

        "valid_from": null,

      }

        "text": "RE-call's DB-backed suite produces failures that have nothing to do with the code under test,\nrepeatedly and at wildly different scales: 15 failed + 5 errors, 473 errors, 41 failed + 59\nerrors, 8 failed + 12 errors, and single one-off errors. Every one passed on isolated re-run.\nBudget for it: the full suite is 15-20 minutes, so a false red is expensive to chase.\n\n## 2026-08-15: the root cause is fixed in the repo. Use the scripts.\n\n`tests/conftest.py` no longer defaults to `localhost:5432`. Unset, `TEST_DSN` points at port 1,\nso an unconfigured run skips loudly instead of silently sharing a database. The manual `docker\nrun` recipe below is now `scripts/session-db.sh`:",
        "source": "recall/concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.805387+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,

        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f **The exception, and only this one: a single DB-free FILE.** 2026-08-15 a reachable but\nschema-incompatible database made `conftest.py`'s session-scoped autouse\n`_bootstrap_default_test_schema` raise out of `apply_migrations`, which **ERRORed every test in the\nrepo**, including files that touch no database. An untouched file errored identically, which is how\nI knew it was not my change. `_db_available()` only skips the bootstrap when the DSN is\n*unreachable*, so the fix was to make it unreachable:\n\nRECALL_TEST_DSN=\"postgresql://nobody:nobody@127.0.0.1:1/none\" python -m pytest tests/<one_file>.py -q",
        "source": "recall/concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",
        "ordinal": 8,

        "text": "Con un DB usa-e-getta (`recall_pytest`, owner `recall_beam`, pgvector 0.8.2): **1429 passed,\n1 failed, 4 skipped**. Runner riusabile: `/opt/recall-fb/run_db_tests.py` \u2014 legge il DSN da\n`/opt/recall-beam/.env`, sostituisce **solo** il nome del DB, blocca `recall_bench`/\n`sentiment_agent`/`postgres`, toglie `RECALL_DSN`, non mette mai la password su una command\nline. \u26a0\ufe0f la suite stessa rifiuta di partire se `RECALL_TEST_DSN == RECALL_DSN` (\u00abthese tests\nDROP TABLES\u00bb).",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference-recall-checkouts-vps2-pinned-2026-07-29.md",
        "ordinal": 11,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:06:22.671367+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5354442277285927,

        "text": "\u26d4 **Never \"isolate\" a DB-free change by pointing the DSN at a dead port.** `_db_available()`\ncovers most of the suite but not all: three `tests/test_bench_systems.py::test_recall_system_*`\ntests FAIL with `psycopg.errors.ConnectionTimeout` instead of skipping, manufacturing a red that\nlooks like your change.",

query.query: can two pytest sessions run at the same time here

rows.payload:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "outcome": "abstained",
  "answer": null,
  "clarification_request": null,
  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "can two pytest sessions run at the same time here",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,
    "decision_state": "supported",
    "calibrated": true,
    "stale": false,
    "embedding_profile": "voyage:voyage-4",
    "retrieval_profile": "fast",
    "index_generation": "legacy",
    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "90b26b8b49c514cb4453caba1d16026b4699144a0810c1a2ff04532c66dfd20a",
        "text": "Two pytest sessions running at the same time against the same test database collide. `tests/conftest.py`\ncalls `apply_migrations` from a session fixture, and `recall.schema`'s guard refuses the second one:\n\nrecall.schema.ConcurrentMigrator: another RE-call schema migrator is already running\n\nThe loser does not fail one test. **Every** test errors at setup, so the run reports e.g.\n`3 skipped, 62 errors` with no failures at all. Reproduced deliberately on 2026-08-05 with three\nconcurrent runs of `tests/test_bench_systems.py`: one passed, two errored wholesale.",
        "source": "recall/pytest-sessions-cannot-run-in-parallel.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:49.845452+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5924287085277622,
        "confidence": 0.9704231697997363,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "8de55c1fd87dbd4e48952d91019be0b4f35ed3ccb3fc0041eb9b4434265deff6",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n1. A suite verdict is the SUMMARY LINE, never an exit code. An output file with no pytest output\n   means \"did not run or was lost\", whatever the code says.\n2. Launch long suites detached with their own log (`nohup python -u -m pytest tests/ -q > log\n   2>&1 &`, the `-u` matters or the log stays empty for minutes) and watch the log with a\n   Monitor until-loop for the summary line.\n3. Before relaunching anything DB-backed, list live python processes and match COMMAND LINES:\n   two suites on one session database invalidate each other silently.\n4. Distinguish your processes from other sessions' by command line before killing: this machine\n   routinely runs parallel sessions with their own suites.",
        "source": "recall/background-suite-exit-0-with-empty-output-is-not-green.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:35.541082+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5672482429894976,
        "confidence": 0.9196177695693883,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "aefa693b11a3901015aa3bd3ffff724f6f3170bb54c08ccb75418c9ad377506f",
        "text": "| Symptom | Cause |\n| --- | --- |\n| `ConcurrentMigrator` in fixture setup | two pytest processes contend for the schema-migration advisory lock; `scripts/ablate_store_latency_guards.py` documents it |\n| `LockNotAvailable: canceling statement due to lock timeout` | another session on the SAME container, still running |\n| `test_rate_limit_http.py`, `test_mcp_auth_http.py` | these stand up real HTTP servers and contend on PORTS; a private container does not protect them |\n| `FileNotFoundError` inside `tmp_path` | pytest keeps only the 3 most recent `pytest-of-<user>/pytest-<n>` roots and prunes older ones AT STARTUP, so a new run deletes the dirs of runs in flight |\n| pool / latency / backend-count assertions (\"pool churned: 3 distinct backends\u2026\") | CPU contention, not DB contention |\n|",
        "source": "recall/concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",
        "ordinal": 14,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.824048+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.537134674958309,
        "confidence": 0.7644409311672008,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "639814e935a0470b83ab54288e94db52693a71cf4f61d955bfb2cfd87701cf45",
        "text": "**Why it matters:** the guard is working as designed, but its failure signature looks exactly like a\ncatastrophic breakage of the code under test. It cost me a wrong conclusion once: in a mutation-testing\nharness I counted two mutants as \"caught\" because the suite went red, when the redness was this\ncollision and not the mutant.\n\n**How to apply:** run pytest sessions in this repo **sequentially**, never overlapping. In any harness\nthat shells out to pytest in a loop, treat `errors` and `failed` as different evidence: only `failed`\nmeans a test caught something. Retry (or abort) on seeing `ConcurrentMigrator` in the output rather\nthan scoring that run. See also [[bench-systems-suite-spends-openrouter-credits]] for the other trap in\nthis same file.\n\n---",
        "source": "recall/pytest-sessions-cannot-run-in-parallel.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:49.847457+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5553669929504434,
        "confidence": 0.8743567076816612,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "874f8bb956559895a95fd86e0116c1ec288ab01b260837b2786c93e76f3fb623",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **The competing process is usually one I started myself.** A `bug-auditor` subagent runs pytest.\nChaining `pytest A && pytest B` overlaps if the first has not fully released its connections. Both\nhappened repeatedly, and I diagnosed the results as broken apparatus, code regression, catalog\nbloat and machine contention before noticing I was the other party. **Tell subagents explicitly not\nto touch the database, and never run a suite while one is live.**\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **The failing test set CHANGES every run** and each one passes in isolation, which reads exactly\nlike order-dependent shared state. There is no randomiser installed \u2014 it is whichever test happened\nto be migrating when the lock was taken.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference-concurrentmigrator-false-failures-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:06:21.234026+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5886054214419616,
        "confidence": 0.9654694750487122,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "2b011a564c4d7bee666544b762d0917291aed1bfe43c6f1ac2c7091fb440dfd9",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f **CI is the arbiter, not this box.** The GitHub runner gets a private database and no competing\nsession; both PRs (#234, #239) went green there on `test` while the local suite still showed\ncollisions. 12 worktrees share this clone \u2192 [[feedback-concurrent-sessions-race-the-same-clone-2026-07-24]].\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **Write the expected pass count BEFORE the run.** \"3115 passed, 0 failed\" reads as success; only\na committed prediction of 3117 made the gap visible, and that gap is what led to this diagnosis.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference-concurrentmigrator-false-failures-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:06:21.242329+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.569634846492428,
        "confidence": 0.9266968471749202,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "0bfb5da020a86a1fb214a049ef3d78014751751687f46028ac89633e6ef4efed",
        "text": "**Moved here 2026-08-15** from the `RE-call` memory store, which forked from this one when the\ndirectory was renamed to `recall`. It sat there unreachable for ten days while I worked the same\nfailure family from the other store. Renaming a project directory silently forks its memory.\n\nThe collision is narrower now but not gone: `scripts/session-db.sh up` gives each checkout its own\ndatabase, so two sessions in *different* checkouts no longer contend for one migrator. Two runs in\nthe *same* checkout still do, because they share a DSN. The reading rule survives intact and is the\ndurable part: **`errors` and `failed` are different evidence, and only `failed` means a test caught\nsomething.** See [[concurrent-pytest-false-reds]].",
        "source": "recall/pytest-sessions-cannot-run-in-parallel.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:49.839302+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5573831464419884,
        "confidence": 0.8833351541294734,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      }
    ],

        "text": "Two pytest sessions running at the same time against the same test database collide. `tests/conftest.py`\ncalls `apply_migrations` from a session fixture, and `recall.schema`'s guard refuses the second one:\n\nrecall.schema.ConcurrentMigrator: another RE-call schema migrator is already running\n\nThe loser does not fail one test. **Every** test errors at setup, so the run reports e.g.\n`3 skipped, 62 errors` with no failures at all.         "text": "**How to apply:**\n1. A suite verdict is the SUMMARY LINE, never an exit code. An output file with no pytest output\n   means \"did not run or was lost\", whatever the code says.\n2.         "text": "| Symptom | Cause |\n| --- | --- |\n| `ConcurrentMigrator` in fixture setup | two pytest processes contend for the schema-migration advisory lock; `scripts/ablate_store_latency_guards.py` documents it |\n| `LockNotAvailable: canceling statement due to lock timeout` | another session on the SAME container, still running |\n| `test_rate_limit_http.py`, `test_mcp_auth_http.py` | these stand up real HTTP servers and contend on PORTS; a private container does not protect them |\n| `FileNotFoundError` inside `tmp_path` | pytest keeps only the 3 most recent `pytest-of-<user>/pytest-<n>` roots and prunes older ones AT STARTUP, so a new run deletes the dirs of runs in flight |\n| pool / latency / backend-count assertions (\"pool churned: 3 distinct backends\u2026\") | CPU contention, not DB contention |\n|",

        "text": "**Why it matters:** the guard is working as designed, but its failure signature looks exactly like a\ncatastrophic breakage of the code under test. It cost me a wrong conclusion once: in a mutation-testing\nharness I counted two mutants as \"caught\" because the suite went red, when the redness was this\ncollision and not the mutant.\n\n**How to apply:** run pytest sessions in this repo **sequentially**, never overlapping.         "text": "**Moved here 2026-08-15** from the `RE-call` memory store, which forked from this one when the\ndirectory was renamed to `recall`.     "query": "what happens if I mix two embedding models in one tenant",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,
    "decision_state": "supported",
    "calibrated": true,
    "stale": false,
    "embedding_profile": "voyage:voyage-4",

      {
        "chunk_id": "f2440fbf349851c02d440bcfe19c1379d678a2bd43d2fe118b0a28ef7c847afc",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **One embedding model per tenant.** Not a convention: it is the only thing standing between a\nmixed corpus and silently wrong retrieval. When a corpus wants a code model and a prose model,\nthat is two tenants, not one with two writers.\n\nFound on 2026-08-15 designing the `recall_repos` corpus on VPS2 (five repositories, code via\n`voyage-code-3`, docs via `voyage-4`). Ten tenants, `<repo>-code` and `<repo>-docs`, for exactly\nthis reason. The index driver asserts `code_embedder.dim == docs_embedder.dim` before writing,\nbecause both tenants share one table and one fixed vector width.\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f The same reasoning applies to the CHUNKER, but the failure is different and worse: see\n[[chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint]]. Related: [[guards-that-cannot-fail]],\n[[recall-corpus-name-boundary]].",
        "source": "recall/mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:45.166042+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6652348837116442,
        "confidence": 0.9985533028779916,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "ad407afb81ffbe3dd2ee8c1e07aded4d624969c80597ee525aca96a496c33bb3",
        "text": "`RetrievalDiagnostics.embedding_profile` (`recall/retriever.py:325`, `:471`) is **reported, never\nenforced**. Nothing in `recall/store.py` filters rows by it: the only occurrence is a `count(*)\nFILTER (WHERE NOT metadata ? 'embedding_profile')` used for a readiness report. So a tenant holding\npassages from two models is not an error state the code can see.\n\nIt is also not a *loud* failure, which is the part that matters. pgvector would reject a dimension\nmismatch, so two models of DIFFERENT width fail fast. The dangerous case is two models of the\n**same** width: `voyage-4` and `voyage-code-3` are both 1024, so a query embedded with one is\ncosine-compared against passages embedded with the other, the SQL succeeds, and the ranking is\ngarbage that looks exactly like a ranking.",
        "source": "recall/mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:45.160230+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.613179523145549,
        "confidence": 0.9873700742945989,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "1bd4ead73b5ee728600f60c0ee6ba3fccfcd5296b5083ab003b1fc865cc9ac61",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **Verify an embedder by `vector_dims(embedding)`, never by the profile label**: at least on\nthe fastembed path. Extends [[mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent]]: the field that was\nsupposed to make mixing detectable is itself inert, so that lesson is stronger than written.\n\nNot filed as a fix yet. The fix is to derive the default `profile_id` from model name plus\ndimension, which re-fingerprints every fastembed corpus, a migration, not a one-liner.",
        "source": "recall/fastembed-profile-id-is-hardcoded.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:40.898460+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5500669151504696,
        "confidence": 0.8479072817176957,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "9bef967347ccfe5e3082962b8e151ebe3d83fab5fef0799dbfafbc620428dcf8",
        "text": "So a live memory search embeds the query with voyage-4 and compares it against 8,716 bge-small\ndocument vectors. **Both models emit 1024 dimensions, so pgvector computes a cosine happily** and\nreturns a confidently ranked list that means nothing. No error, no warning, no failure code that\nnames it.\n\nRe-measure (the profile lives in the row's metadata, and mixing shows up as more than one value):\n\n```bash\npsql \"$RECALL_DSN\" -c \"SELECT tenant_id, metadata->>'embedding_profile' AS profile, count(*) \\\n  FROM chunks GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,3 DESC;\"\nssh vps2 \"ps -eo args | grep -o 'RECALL_TENANT=[^ ]* RECALL_EMBEDDER=[^ ]*' | sort -u\"\n```",
        "source": "recall/vps2-memory-tenant-mixes-three-embedders.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:02.180439+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5383456945419349,
        "confidence": 0.7734426356504502,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "345f3c331a1bbf8c16dea66bd35f6eaee82bfd829a8aa18be0f305946a4260d4",
        "text": "reported\r\n`corpus: 9552 chunks, 0 of them keyed by a Windows path`, so the adoption held across a day and\r\na further sync. The hazard is closed; this memo is now about the MECHANISM, which recurs\r\nwherever a corpus moves hosts, rather than about an open task.\r\n\r\n**The tenant's other defect was fixed in the same session, in the other direction from the one this\r\nmemo assumed.** It held two profiles at once (6,392 `bge-small-symmetric-v1`, 3,060 bge-large) while\r\nthe client queried it with `voyage-4`, so the corpus was re-embedded with **voyage-4** rather than\r\nthe client being pointed at bge-large: the sibling tenants already use it, and the alternative puts\r\na 1.4 GB ONNX model inside every stdio server session on that host. See\r\n[[vps2-memory-tenant-mixes-three-embedders]].",
        "source": "recall/vps2-memory-corpus-is-keyed-by-windows-paths.md",

Fixing a chunker-selection bug therefore does\n**not** repair an affected corpus by re-running `recall index`, the run reports \"N unchanged\" and\nleaves every wrongly-split chunk exactly where it was.\n\nTo actually rebuild, change one of the three terms (a different embedder, a different context\npolicy) or delete the affected sources first and let the next run re-read them.\n\nThe source docstring calls widening the tuple out as a migration rather than a comment change,\nbecause it re-fingerprints every indexed corpus at once.         "text": "own corpus; shipped as designed in `recall setup`.\n- [Data as literals becomes corpus](data-as-literals-becomes-corpus.md) \u2014 the off-topic pool lived in a `.py` and so disqualified all 25 of its own subjects in any code corpus rooted here; a dogfood failure, not a user one.\n- [Chunker is not in the index fingerprint](chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint.md) \u2014 fixing a chunker bug does NOT repair the corpus; a re-index reports \"unchanged\" and leaves every wrong split in place.\n- [CI runs are silently not created](ci-runs-are-silently-not-created.md) \u2014 a dropped webhook means NO run; `gh pr checks` then serves the PREVIOUS run's job ids, so absent looks exactly like green.\n- [CI flake cluster: the ordering index served the unservable](ci-flake-cluster-planner-and-generations-tests.md) \u2014",

        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.533097505569458,
        "confidence": 0.7326802408115715,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "47112135e2d9609b19470dcd40d54918f486c17419443b2ee34441310271f148",
        "text": "Found on 2026-08-15 fixing `recall index`, which chose the chunker from the GLOB SUFFIX\n(`chunk_code if args.glob.endswith(\".py\") else chunk_text`) rather than per file, so\n`--glob '**/*'` chunked every `.py` as prose and said nothing. Do not widen `PYTHON_SUFFIXES` without a\nchunker that parses the language being added.\n\n## Two consequences measured 2026-08-18",

        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:37.231143+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.540107011795044,
        "confidence": 0.7860954963151302,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {

        "text": "Measured 2026-08-19, in recall's own memory corpus, using recall itself.\n\nA memo carried a \ud83d\udd01 correction at the top of the file retracting a claim in its middle. Searching\nfor that claim returned **the falsified paragraph on its own**, as chunk ordinal 7, with no trace of\nthe correction: retrieval returns **chunks**, and the correction was in a different one.\n\nThe second attempt failed too, and this is the part worth keeping. I inserted a \u26d4 retraction\nparagraph **immediately above** the falsified block, re-indexed, and re-ran the query. The chunker\ndoes not split on paragraph boundaries, so the retraction landed in the neighbouring chunk again and\nthe claim still came back naked.",

        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:31.819702+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5598692560273862,
        "confidence": 0.8936349919498356,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"

        "confidence": 0.6027907154887057,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "5dd726267227a8517426d6c7ae55a68885591891f356365f4413b6d4321d43a7",
        "text": "- VPS2 dense plus lexical crashed at `53,611` chunks / `47,009` docs on a NUL byte in EnterpriseRAG document `dsid_e0bd1843e132405186f39bf178fc12c4`.\n- Commit `60f5447` scrubs NUL bytes during official text ZIP ingestion.\n- Commit `ecdff60` adds `--skip-indexed-sources`, allowing partial benchmark indexes to resume by skipping source ids already present in the table.\n- VPS2 was restarted with `--skip-indexed-sources`, `batch_chunks=24`, table `ber_voy_lex_12k_full`, tenant `enterprise-rag-voyage-lexical-chunk12k-full`, output `results/enterprise_rag/vps2_voyage_lexical_chunk12k_full.answers.jsonl`, log `logs/enterprise_rag_vps2_lexical_chunk12k_resume.log`, pid file `enterprise_rag_vps2_lexical_resume.pid`.\n- It printed `index resume existing_sources=47009`, moved past the old crash, and",

        "text": "**The chunker is not in it.** So a file whose bytes have not changed is skipped even when the\nchunker that would now read it is a different one. Fixing a chunker-selection bug therefore does\n**not** repair an affected corpus by re-running `recall index`, the run reports \"N unchanged\" and\nleaves every wrongly-split chunk exactly where it was.\n\nTo actually rebuild, change one of the three terms (a different embedder, a different context\npolicy) or delete the affected sources first and let the next run re-read them.\n\nThe source docstring calls widening the tuple out as a migration rather than a comment change,\nbecause it re-fingerprints every indexed corpus at once. That is a real cost and the reason it has\nnot been done, not an oversight.",
        "source": "recall/chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:37.229499+00:00",

      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "a3cd442d2c67a007fddda0eabb8cc6979d4c750af7dfca9ec86dfb399125de94",
        "text": "own corpus; shipped as designed in `recall setup`.\n- [Data as literals becomes corpus](data-as-literals-becomes-corpus.md) \u2014 the off-topic pool lived in a `.py` and so disqualified all 25 of its own subjects in any code corpus rooted here; a dogfood failure, not a user one.\n- [Chunker is not in the index fingerprint](chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint.md) \u2014 fixing a chunker bug does NOT repair the corpus; a re-index reports \"unchanged\" and leaves every wrong split in place.\n- [CI runs are silently not created](ci-runs-are-silently-not-created.md) \u2014 a dropped webhook means NO run; `gh pr checks` then serves the PREVIOUS run's job ids, so absent looks exactly like green.\n- [CI flake cluster: the ordering index served the unservable](ci-flake-cluster-planner-and-generations-tests.md) \u2014",
        "source": "recall/project_index.md",
        "ordinal": 7,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:48.355819+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5324216206325076,
        "confidence": 0.7271050667564398,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "47112135e2d9609b19470dcd40d54918f486c17419443b2ee34441310271f148",
        "text": "Found on 2026-08-15 fixing `recall index`, which chose the chunker from the GLOB SUFFIX\n(`chunk_code if args.glob.endswith(\".py\") else chunk_text`) rather than per file, so\n`--glob '**/*'` chunked every `.py` as prose and said nothing. Fixed by `chunker_for_path`, with\nthe non-repair noted in its docstring so the next person does not assume a re-index is enough.\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f `chunk_code` is **Python-specific**: it starts a block at a column-0 `def`/`class`/`@`/`async\ndef`. Given Rust, SQL or shell it matches nothing, returns one block, and is strictly worse than\n`chunk_text`, which at least splits on blank lines. Do not widen `PYTHON_SUFFIXES` without a\nchunker that parses the language being added.\n\n## Two consequences measured 2026-08-18",
        "source": "recall/chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:37.231143+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5392997586309776,
        "confidence": 0.7803611686593174,
        "verdict": "ok",

      },

Searching\nfor that claim returned **the falsified paragraph on its own**, as chunk ordinal 7, with no trace of\nthe correction: retrieval returns **chunks**, and the correction was in a different one.\n\nThe second attempt failed too, and this is the part worth keeping. I inserted a \u26d4 retraction\nparagraph **immediately above** the falsified block, re-indexed, and re-ran the query. The chunker\ndoes not split on paragraph boundaries, so the retraction landed in the neighbouring chunk again and\nthe claim still came back naked.",

        "text": "own corpus; shipped as designed in `recall setup`.\n- [Data as literals becomes corpus](data-as-literals-becomes-corpus.md) \u2014 the off-topic pool lived in a `.py` and so disqualified all 25 of its own subjects in any code corpus rooted here; a dogfood failure, not a user one.\n- [Chunker is not in the index fingerprint](chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint.md) \u2014 fixing a chunker bug does NOT repair the corpus; a re-index reports \"unchanged\" and leaves every wrong split in place.\n- [CI runs are silently not created](ci-runs-are-silently-not-created.md) \u2014 a dropped webhook means NO run; `gh pr checks` then serves the PREVIOUS run's job ids, so absent looks exactly like green.\n- [CI flake cluster: the ordering index served the unservable](ci-flake-cluster-planner-and-generations-tests.md) \u2014",

        "text": "Found on 2026-08-15 fixing `recall index`, which chose the chunker from the GLOB SUFFIX\n(`chunk_code if args.glob.endswith(\".py\") else chunk_text`) rather than per file, so\n`--glob '**/*'` chunked every `.py` as prose and said nothing.       {
        "chunk_id": "d4dfd992915833ac3e6ee6ee4f2a704e6c60b566cd8690b3a4b5f42b2faa598e",
        "text": "RE-call has never been run through `ruff format`. As of 2026-08-08, `python -m ruff format --check .`\nreports **348 of 406 files would be reformatted**. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs only\n`ruff check .` plus bare `mypy`. `pyproject.toml` sets `[tool.ruff] line-length = 100` and nothing\nelse about formatting.\n\n**Why:** a `ruff format --check` failure on a file I am touching looks like a defect I introduced or\na nit worth clearing. It is neither. It is the repo's baseline state. I flagged one as a nit and\n\"fixed\" it, which imposed an unused convention on one arbitrary file and put two unrelated hunks\ninto a diff that was supposed to be eight lines of test markers.",
        "source": "recall/ruff-format-is-not-this-repos-convention.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:52.991220+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6837074160575867,
        "confidence": 0.9993315856979627,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "8d70fe73664017ac2001119e41fc7ef89028ac8cdb4eb798177ef34966fcbc3f",
        "text": "**How to apply:** run `python -m ruff check` to gate my work, never `ruff format`. If a format\nfailure appears on a file I edited, confirm it predates me (`git stash` then re-check) and leave it.\nReformatting is a repo-wide decision for the user, not a side effect of an unrelated change.\n\nRelated: [[ruff-blocked-locally]] for why it must be `python -m ruff` and not bare `ruff`.",
        "source": "recall/ruff-format-is-not-this-repos-convention.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:53.008323+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6536973714828491,
        "confidence": 0.9976577150648109,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "7abb32337e2f444abeba1813d1ed5b0277d43888517fab7e434e35df0276c89e",
        "text": "and the merged follow-up banner fix in PR #368.\n- [ruff format is not this repo's convention](ruff-format-is-not-this-repos-convention.md) \u2014 348/406 files fail it; CI runs `ruff check` only, so never reformat.\n- [ruff runs here after all](ruff-blocked-locally.md) \u2014 CORRECTED: `python -m ruff` works (0.16.2, matches the repo pin); bare `ruff` is an old 0.6.9.\n- [session-db orphans reports a false clean](session-db-orphans-false-clean.md) \u2014 prints \"no orphaned containers\" when `docker` is not on PATH, and it fires exactly during session-close.\n- [Shared editable install across worktrees](shared-editable-install-across-worktrees.md) \u2014 one pip install serves ~18 worktrees; `python -m recall` from an unrelated dir silently runs the wrong checkout.\n- [Spawned task chips duplicate",
        "source": "recall/project_index.md",
        "ordinal": 17,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:48.477467+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5970328628132603,
        "confidence": 0.9754786326422918,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "b0c3a3df91ba0bbf87e00e802345f4c25190930eb124e7e137658098b76a11a3",
        "text": "*is* mypy), and then say \"blocked locally,\r\ngated in CI\" rather than \"mypy skipped\": a green CI job is a passing typecheck with an unusual\r\nevidence path, not a missing gate.\r\n\r\nRelated, still true: `ruff format --check` reports ~251 files would be reformatted in RE-call, and\r\nthat is **not a gate** \u2014 CI runs `ruff check` only. Separately the repo pins `ruff>=0.5,<0.16`\r\nbecause 0.16 stabilised new rules, so a local ruff 0.16 reports ~339 errors on unchanged code;\r\nconfirm a lint finding is yours by re-running with your changes stashed before reporting it.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udd11 The general form, which is why this file now leads with a warning instead of a fact:\r\n**a memory asserting \"X cannot be done\" is the most expensive kind to leave unverified**, because\r\nit stops you retrying and so can never correct",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference-mypy-blocked-by-windows-app-control-2026-08-04.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:06:22.259152+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5544075304976108,
        "confidence": 0.8698798306745273,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "ebce158b9fd788681d4862244a1535b09ae33d91b334f7c9c0fbc7414cb5972b",
        "text": "Measured 2026-08-29 on PR #13: `ruff check .` printed \"All checks passed!\" here and CI went red in\n9 seconds, twice, on four findings the older binary does not know about (TRY004, RUF100 twice,\nI001).\n\nThe cause is two ruffs. `requirements-dev.txt` pins **ruff 0.16.2**, which is what CI installs and\nwhat `python -m ruff` resolves to in this checkout. The `ruff` on PATH is **0.6.9**, stale, and its\ndefault rule set is narrower. Both answer to the same command name, neither says which it is, and\nthe newer one is the one that decides whether the branch is mergeable.\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f The `ruff check .` line in this repository's own docs and in the CI workflow is therefore a\ntrap when read as a local instruction. Run it as a module:\n\n```bash\npython -m ruff check . && python -m ruff --version\n```",
        "source": "agent-memory-bench/pinned-ruff-is-not-the-one-on-path.md",

        "text": "- **Before renaming a project directory**, move `~/.claude/projects/<old-slug>/memory/` into the new\n  slug. Do it at rename time; there is no later signal that anything is missing.\n- **When a memory store looks thin for a project with history**, list `~/.claude/projects/` and look\n  for a slug matching an old name of the directory. Two stores for one project is the tell.\n- The same key derivation strands stores when a **user profile** changes: 533 memos under\n  `C--Users-temen-*` belong to a Windows profile that no longer exists.\n\nArchived, not deleted, at `~/.claude/archive/stranded-memory-stores-2026-08-15/`, with a README\nrecording what was recovered and what was deliberately left unmerged.",
        "source": "recall/renaming-a-project-forks-its-memory.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:52.608890+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6748328998784494,

        "text": "`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/` is keyed on the **project path**. Rename the directory and a\nfresh, empty store appears under the new slug. The old one keeps every memo and becomes invisible:\nno error, no warning, and the index you load each session is simply the new empty one.\n\n**Why:** discovered 2026-08-15 auditing memory fragmentation. `Documents/RE-call` had been renamed\nto `Documents/recall`, leaving `C--Users-gde00-Documents-RE-call/memory/` with two real memos:\n\n- `pytest-sessions-cannot-run-in-parallel` (written 2026-08-05)\n- `bench-systems-suite-spends-openrouter-credits`",
        "source": "recall/renaming-a-project-forks-its-memory.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:52.595982+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6882652454534331,
        "confidence": 0.9994475736651552,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "2cacceeb0843865dcbf4c6a850a68068ffe14dd0354cdfdf2938628648b10ae2",
        "text": "session landed 11 of my 12 commits; also closes/rebases PRs under you, and a stale base looks exactly like a regression.\n- [Renaming a project forks its memory](renaming-a-project-forks-its-memory.md) \u2014 the store key is the PATH; the RE-call rename hid two memos for ten days while I worked the same bug from the other half.\n- [Guards placed after the action](guards-placed-after-the-action.md) \u2014 I wrote the token file THEN checked it was ignored, with the right invariant in the comment above the wrong code; a mutation test proves a guard fires, not that it fires in time.\n- [Blockers outlive their cause](blockers-outlive-their-cause.md) \u2014 a spec sat at \"blocked on VPS2\" for 13 days after VPS2 recovered; pair a block with the condition that clears it, and date one against the world before",
        "source": "recall/feedback_index.md",
        "ordinal": 16,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:41.067907+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5105874830134233,
        "confidence": 0.5165993684504792,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "e22f67fc6ce72963b5d1f7dcc6297152bed647e35ed81e706b8cb4276c3af9d6",
        "text": "Corollary worth carrying: the entry is keyed by path at all, so **moving or renaming the project\norphans whatever is under it**, silently. Same shape as the memory-store forking described in\n`CLAUDE.md`. Re-run the installer after a move, and print the key that was registered.",

  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "what happens to a project's memory when I rename its directory",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,

    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "48cd032dae9004ca082970d53a0a71b625b191ba0713485b2dac4f605224cf8c",
        "text": "- **Before renaming a project directory**, move `~/.claude/projects/<old-slug>/memory/` into the new\n  slug. Do it at rename time; there is no later signal that anything is missing.\n- **When a memory store looks thin for a project with history**, list `~/.claude/projects/` and look\n  for a slug matching an old name of the directory. Two stores for one project is the tell.\n- The same key derivation strands stores when a **user profile** changes: 533 memos under\n  `C--Users-temen-*` belong to a Windows profile that no longer exists.\n\nArchived, not deleted, at `~/.claude/archive/stranded-memory-stores-2026-08-15/`, with a README\nrecording what was recovered and what was deliberately left unmerged.",
        "source": "recall/renaming-a-project-forks-its-memory.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:52.608890+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6748328998784494,
        "confidence": 0.9990313277120744,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "ea2b5170f2ec62df8b489ed393a37a4a4277fc751c83550e630d1b9102dc7d58",
        "text": "`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/` is keyed on the **project path**. Rename the directory and a\nfresh, empty store appears under the new slug. The old one keeps every memo and becomes invisible:\nno error, no warning, and the index you load each session is simply the new empty one.\n\n**Why:** discovered 2026-08-15 auditing memory fragmentation. `Documents/RE-call` had been renamed\nto `Documents/recall`, leaving `C--Users-gde00-Documents-RE-call/memory/` with two real memos:\n\n- `pytest-sessions-cannot-run-in-parallel` (written 2026-08-05)\n- `bench-systems-suite-spends-openrouter-credits`",
        "source": "recall/renaming-a-project-forks-its-memory.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:52.595982+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6882652454534331,
        "confidence": 0.9994475736651552,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "2cacceeb0843865dcbf4c6a850a68068ffe14dd0354cdfdf2938628648b10ae2",
        "text": "session landed 11 of my 12 commits; also closes/rebases PRs under you, and a stale base looks exactly like a regression.\n- [Renaming a project forks its memory](renaming-a-project-forks-its-memory.md) \u2014 the store key is the PATH; the RE-call rename hid two memos for ten days while I worked the same bug from the other half.\n- [Guards placed after the action](guards-placed-after-the-action.md) \u2014 I wrote the token file THEN checked it was ignored, with the right invariant in the comment above the wrong code; a mutation test proves a guard fires, not that it fires in time.\n- [Blockers outlive their cause](blockers-outlive-their-cause.md) \u2014 a spec sat at \"blocked on VPS2\" for 13 days after VPS2 recovered; pair a block with the condition that clears it, and date one against the world before",
        "source": "recall/feedback_index.md",
        "ordinal": 16,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:41.067907+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5105874830134233,
        "confidence": 0.5165993684504792,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "e22f67fc6ce72963b5d1f7dcc6297152bed647e35ed81e706b8cb4276c3af9d6",
        "text": "Corollary worth carrying: the entry is keyed by path at all, so **moving or renaming the project\norphans whatever is under it**, silently. Same shape as the memory-store forking described in\n`CLAUDE.md`. Re-run the installer after a move, and print the key that was registered.",
        "source": "recall/claude-project-keys-are-not-normalised.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:37.894339+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6689338684082031,
        "confidence": 0.9987604835592059,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      }
    ],

        "text": "As of 2026-08-12 this repo has ~18 worktrees. The main checkout at\n`C:/Users/gde00/Documents/recall` usually sits on a feature branch (`codex/enterprise-rag-bench`\nwhen this was written), and **`master` is checked out in a separate worktree at\n`C:/Users/gde00/Documents/recall-suite-fix`**.\n\nSo `git checkout master` from the main checkout fails with *\"'master' is already used by worktree\nat ...\"*. To land work on master, operate on that worktree directly:\n\n```bash\ngit -C \"C:/Users/gde00/Documents/recall-suite-fix\" merge --squash <branch>\n```",
        "source": "recall/master-lives-in-a-separate-worktree.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:44.071158+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6026479242653903,
        "confidence": 0.9805129018555708,
        "verdict": "ok",

      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "4ae396f7799e757ba2f55a2f1dfb6d3fe2f1f177d11731a5febdbe4373914d92",
        "text": "**Why this bit me:** I ran `git checkout master 2>&1 | tail -2 && git merge --squash <branch>`. The\npipe made `&&` read `tail`'s exit status, not the failed checkout's, so the squash merge ran against\nthe *feature branch* that happened to be checked out, leaving 13 staged additions and two\nconflicted files in the user's working tree. `git reset --hard HEAD` restored it because nothing was\ncommitted and the tree had been clean.\n\n**How to apply:** Check `git worktree list` before assuming any branch can be checked out. Never\npipe a command whose exit status gates a `&&` chain; capture the status explicitly instead. And\ncheck the target worktree is clean before merging into it.",
        "source": "recall/master-lives-in-a-separate-worktree.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:44.098338+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5163062810897827,
        "confidence": 0.5758358565318726,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "729ad74ba44fe2c474b19c1211aa99a42d305cc4b99b86900552a34312a701f0",
        "text": "local master, the branch ref stayed\n  at the old tip, and `git push` silently pushed **master's tip under the branch name** \u2014 surfacing\n  only as `gh pr create` \u2192 *\"No commits between master and \u2026\"*. An earlier edit to `checks.py` was\n  reverted the same way mid-session. **Check `git branch --show-current` immediately before commit\n  and push, and verify the remote ref with `git ls-remote` after.**\n  Cf. [[feedback-concurrent-sessions-race-the-same-clone-2026-07-24]].\n- \ud83d\udd11 **Fixing a doc can make it false.** LIMITS.md said \"checked 2026-07-31, master is NOT\n  protected\" \u2014 true when written, false ninety minutes later.         "text": "As of 2026-08-12 this repo has ~18 worktrees. The main checkout at\n`C:/Users/gde00/Documents/recall` usually sits on a feature branch (`codex/enterprise-rag-bench`\nwhen this was written), and **`master` is checked out in a separate worktree at\n`C:/Users/gde00/Documents/recall-suite-fix`**.\n\nSo `git checkout master` from the main checkout fails with *\"'master' is already used by worktree\nat ...\"*. To land work on master, operate on that worktree directly:\n\n```bash\ngit -C \"C:/Users/gde00/Documents/recall-suite-fix\" merge --squash <branch>\n```",
        "source": "recall/master-lives-in-a-separate-worktree.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:44.071158+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6026479242653903,
        "confidence": 0.9805129018555708,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "4ae396f7799e757ba2f55a2f1dfb6d3fe2f1f177d11731a5febdbe4373914d92",
        "text": "**Why this bit me:** I ran `git checkout master 2>&1 | tail -2 && git merge --squash <branch>`. The\npipe made `&&` read `tail`'s exit status, not the failed checkout's, so the squash merge ran against\nthe *feature branch* that happened to be checked out, leaving 13 staged additions and two\nconflicted files in the user's working tree. `git reset --hard HEAD` restored it because nothing was\ncommitted and the tree had been clean.\n\n**How to apply:** Check `git worktree list` before assuming any branch can be checked out. Never\npipe a command whose exit status gates a `&&` chain; capture the status explicitly instead. And\ncheck the target worktree is clean before merging into it.",
        "source": "recall/master-lives-in-a-separate-worktree.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:44.098338+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,

        "confidence": 0.5758358565318726,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "729ad74ba44fe2c474b19c1211aa99a42d305cc4b99b86900552a34312a701f0",
        "text": "local master, the branch ref stayed\n  at the old tip, and `git push` silently pushed **master's tip under the branch name** \u2014 surfacing\n  only as `gh pr create` \u2192 *\"No commits between master and \u2026\"*. An earlier edit to `checks.py` was\n  reverted the same way mid-session. **Check `git branch --show-current` immediately before commit\n  and push, and verify the remote ref with `git ls-remote` after.**\n  Cf. [[feedback-concurrent-sessions-race-the-same-clone-2026-07-24]].\n- \ud83d\udd11 **Fixing a doc can make it false.** LIMITS.md said \"checked 2026-07-31, master is NOT\n  protected\" \u2014 true when written, false ninety minutes later. PR #31 exists only to correct the\n  claim the previous PR introduced. A dated, confidently-stated fact needs an owner.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/project-mem-bench-adversarial-review-hardening-2026-07-31.md",
        "ordinal": 14,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:33.726199+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5408033406255648,
        "confidence": 0.7909537056483696,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "dcb0f7dc0ac15e6e3c6d003c435605a8b763d2a5fb95a37135a49b95cbe38e10",
        "text": "2. **`master` moved under a long-running session.** Two PRs (#1 quick-wins, #2 medium-effort)\n   implementing the *same* external audit landed from another session while work was in flight,\n   so a branch cut from `f72ac3e` conflicted. Check `git fetch` before assuming a branch base is\n   current on a repo with parallel sessions.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/project-recall-v040-cca-hardening-2026-07-21.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:40.066597+00:00",

        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **Because master is parked in a worktree nobody routinely pulls, the LOCAL `master` ref is\nusually stale. Compare against `origin/master`, never `master`.** 2026-08-15 this nearly produced a\nbadly wrong report: `git log master..HEAD` said my branch was **24 commits** ahead and I was about\nto tell the user a PR would drag 18 unrelated commits along.       {
        "chunk_id": "bac25f19474642109d42944aa9c0c4799192203d267492e8330b9ba8914a85bc",
        "text": "Un guard non \u00e8 finito quando i suoi controlli passano. \u00c8 finito quando la cosa che **restituisce**\nsoddisfa ancora quei controlli.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-hold-on-its-own-output-2026-08-05.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:13.987838+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6274954080581665,
        "confidence": 0.9930218363849331,
        "verdict": "ok",

      {

        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 The sharper version of the standing lesson: *a guard that reads as protection and cannot fire*\nhas a twin \u2014 **a guard that cannot PASS**. Both look like rigour in a document and neither tests\nanything. Asking \"what would make this fire?\" catches the first; **\"what would make this pass?\"**\nis the question I was not asking.\n\n## What it cost, and what caught it\n\n`bug-auditor` caught F3 (before publication) and would have caught C4; D1 I caught only because I\nran the check anyway. The direct cost was a verdict claiming a \"textbook\" control that was 96%\narithmetic, and a FALSIFIED verdict on a perfectly valid run. **Two of three were caught before\nanything shipped \u2014 by the audit, not by me.**",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-check-the-deciding-cell-has-power-2026-08-06.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:15.827969+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6177338221390504,
        "confidence": 0.9895384532711776,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "eec41629f616f5a2ff7265198388f4308798a1baca5e0f6cc67b3a0011974d1d",
        "text": "**Why:** [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] covers guards that never fire because the assertion was\nunsatisfiable or too narrow from the start. This is the adjacent failure: a guard that used to\nfire, and quietly stops, because it depends on a string/event contract nobody versioned. The\nguard-test in that memory (mutate and watch it go red) catches the first kind but not this one,\nbecause the mutation target is the code under test, not the upstream tool the gate depends on.",

        "ordinal": 1,

        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5983068525286573,
        "confidence": 0.9767218870423391,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "2527d537b7feb48b38cd3b69bf0811d7ed45eddc79376caae313433656152d0b",
        "text": "**Why:** the credibility of a guard is a shared resource. Every false alarm spends it, and it is\nspent silently, so the guard still looks installed long after it stopped being believed.\n\n**How to apply:** when a guard contradicts something you have directly observed, treat that as a\nbug report against the guard and open its source before dismissing it.         "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f Note the asymmetry that makes this dangerous: a cannot-fail guard produces a **false green**,\nand a cannot-pass guard produces a **false red** that discards good work. I produced one of each in\nthe same session.\n\nRelated: [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] (the twin) \u00b7\n[[feedback-a-guard-must-hold-on-its-own-output-2026-08-05]] \u00b7\n[[project-recall-mtrag-retrieval-coverage-bottleneck-2026-08-06]] (where all three occurred)",

        "text": "- Prefer the Edit tool for file changes; it does not do this.\n- If scripting an edit in Python, pass `newline=\"\\n\"`:\n  `path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\\n\")`.\n- To diagnose: `git ls-files --eol <file>` shows index vs working-tree endings directly.\n- To confirm a diff is line-endings-only, hash both sides normalised rather than trusting\n  `git diff --ignore-all-space`, which also hides real whitespace changes:\n  `git show HEAD:f | tr -d '\\r' | sha256sum` against `tr -d '\\r' < f | sha256sum`.\n- To fix once content is confirmed identical: `git checkout -- <files>`. Do NOT commit it; the\n  commit would record no content change.\n\nRelated: [[ruff-blocked-locally]] for the other local tooling gotcha in this repo.",
        "source": "recall/python-write-text-crlf-churn.md",
        "ordinal": 1,

        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f Same session, a second way a \"successful\" write leaves the wrong state, unrelated to concurrency.\r\nMy mutation harness restored each file with `path.write_text(original)` and verified the restore by\r\ncomparing a hash of `read_text`. It passed. `git status` still showed the file **modified**: on\r\nWindows `write_text` had converted the whole file **LF \u2192 CRLF**, and `read_text` universalises\r\nnewlines on read, so the hash could not see what the write had done. Had I committed, the diff would\r\nhave been every line of `recall/lineage.py`.\r\n\ud83d\udd11 **A hash taken through a normalising read cannot verify a write.** Verify a restore with\r\n`git diff --stat` (or `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol` to separate content from endings), not with a\r\nchecksum you computed yourself. Same family as *diff the file",

        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f Same session, a second way a \"successful\" write leaves the wrong state, unrelated to concurrency.\r\nMy mutation harness restored each file with `path.write_text(original)` and verified the restore by\r\ncomparing a hash of `read_text`.         "valid_from": null,

        "verdict": "ok",

        "text": "**Why:** on 2026-08-05 one sentence in RE-call's `ENTERPRISE_PROGRAM_STATUS.md` asserting an\nintegrity check was wrong **four times**: a digest of the pre-rewrite script; a test-file digest\nthat moved when one test was appended; the CRLF/LF boundary above; and finally staleness inside its\nown commit.         "confidence": 0.679620039108006,

        "text": "Writing a literal U+2028 into a Python test file via the editing tools is unreliable.         "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f Same session, a second way a \"successful\" write leaves the wrong state, unrelated to concurrency.\r\nMy mutation harness restored each file with `path.write_text(original)` and verified the restore by\r\ncomparing a hash of `read_text`.         "valid_from": null,

        "text": "**Why:** on 2026-08-05 one sentence in RE-call's `ENTERPRISE_PROGRAM_STATUS.md` asserting an\nintegrity check was wrong **four times**: a digest of the pre-rewrite script; a test-file digest\nthat moved when one test was appended; the CRLF/LF boundary above; and finally staleness inside its\nown commit.         "valid_from": null,

        "confidence": 0.679620039108006,

        "authority": "unknown"

        "text": "Writing a literal U+2028 into a Python test file via the editing tools is unreliable.       {

        "text": "- Prefer the Edit tool for file changes; it does not do this.\n- If scripting an edit in Python, pass `newline=\"\\n\"`:\n  `path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\", newline=\"\\n\")`.\n- To diagnose: `git ls-files --eol <file>` shows index vs working-tree endings directly.\n- To confirm a diff is line-endings-only, hash both sides normalised rather than trusting\n  `git diff --ignore-all-space`, which also hides real whitespace changes:\n  `git show HEAD:f | tr -d '\\r' | sha256sum` against `tr -d '\\r' < f | sha256sum`.\n- To fix once content is confirmed identical: `git checkout -- <files>`. Do NOT commit it; the\n  commit would record no content change.\n\nRelated: [[ruff-blocked-locally]] for the other local tooling gotcha in this repo.",
        "source": "recall/python-write-text-crlf-churn.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:49.908049+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.615793989206077,
        "confidence": 0.9886639631811434,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "c5c2a03b5b79f244f3efe8069a5992d87f4c6e6d774fb0a8ffaa23daa7f66083",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f Same session, a second way a \"successful\" write leaves the wrong state, unrelated to concurrency.\r\nMy mutation harness restored each file with `path.write_text(original)` and verified the restore by\r\ncomparing a hash of `read_text`. It passed. `git status` still showed the file **modified**: on\r\nWindows `write_text` had converted the whole file **LF \u2192 CRLF**, and `read_text` universalises\r\nnewlines on read, so the hash could not see what the write had done. Had I committed, the diff would\r\nhave been every line of `recall/lineage.py`.\r\n\ud83d\udd11 **A hash taken through a normalising read cannot verify a write.** Verify a restore with\r\n`git diff --stat` (or `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol` to separate content from endings), not with a\r\nchecksum you computed yourself. Same family as *diff the file",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-concurrent-sessions-race-the-same-clone-2026-07-24.md",
        "ordinal": 30,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:16.076122+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6109291315078779,
        "confidence": 0.9861403537114042,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "eda6c34066b95c6fa7aaab16e2f773cf9abd7aecc5a6d38c408031b9e4aa71b7",
        "text": "This repo's `.gitattributes` sets `* text=auto eol=lf`, so the working tree is meant to be LF\neven on Windows. `Path.write_text(...)` in Python's default text mode translates `\\n` to `\\r\\n`\non Windows, so any file edited that way comes back as CRLF and git reports it modified forever,\nwith `warning: CRLF will be replaced by LF` on every add.\n\nObserved 2026-08-07: after a session of scripted edits, `git status` showed `recall/retriever.py`\nand `recall/store.py` as modified with **zero content difference**. `git ls-files --eol` showed\n`i/lf w/crlf`, i.e. index LF, working tree CRLF.\n\n**How to apply:**",
        "source": "recall/python-write-text-crlf-churn.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:49.894091+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.600415110588078,
        "confidence": 0.9786453545907314,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "058706caa517c5de109520464c2a0bc9bce6d2f58f153cc675fcf01194607db0",
        "text": "**Why:** on 2026-08-05 one sentence in RE-call's `ENTERPRISE_PROGRAM_STATUS.md` asserting an\nintegrity check was wrong **four times**: a digest of the pre-rewrite script; a test-file digest\nthat moved when one test was appended; the CRLF/LF boundary above; and finally staleness inside its\nown commit. The first three corrections all patched the number. **Four rounds on one claim means\nthe mechanism is wrong, not the value**, and this was three rounds of treating a mechanism failure\nas an arithmetic one, in a document whose argument is that undemonstrated claims are the failure\nmode. The same class from the other side: a mutation harness whose `write_text` restore rewrote LF\nas CRLF and left ten files dirty with no content diff.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference-working-copy-vs-git-blob-crlf-boundary-2026-08-05.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:06:23.606073+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5269734263420143,
        "confidence": 0.679620039108006,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "aa28ce5b43aae822c5035488423733e75eb7b6d8a1ece56245f15858dcc92b29",
        "text": "Writing a literal U+2028 into a Python test file via the editing tools is unreliable. On\n2026-08-11, in `tests/test_fix.py`, the same pasted character survived in one test and was\nsilently turned into an ordinary space (U+0020) in two others written minutes later.\n\n**Why it matters more than it sounds:** the affected tests were guards ABOUT line separators. With\nthe separator flattened to a space, one guard passed against the unfixed code and another failed\nagainst the fixed code, that is, the results inverted. Nothing in the pytest output looked wrong;\nonly dumping the source's actual code points found it. This is [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] arriving\nthrough the editor rather than through the assertion.",
        "source": "recall/pasted-unicode-separators-rot.md",

That is the failure mode to watch\nfor: not an error, a wrong corpus.\n\n## What was actually missing: recall did not dogfood itself\n\nrecall ships an MCP server (`recall_mcp`, 10 tools) and `docs/USING_WITH_CLAUDE.md` documents\nexactly how to install it. The project did not use it on itself. It does now:",

        "text": "Measured 2026-08-16, by probing every server directly over MCP streamable HTTP\nrather than by opinion:\n\n- **All five internal servers are live and reachable** on the tailnet.\n  `qwen-mcp` is `qwen-agent 1.27.0` with **33 tools**.\n- `code_search`, `db_query_ro` and `rg_search_live` all returned correct results\n  **first try, with correct arguments**. So 37 of 41 sessions began with no MCP servers at all.",

        "text": "\u2705 **M2 COMPLETE 2026-07-07** (self-recall MCP loop). `recall_mcp` FastMCP server over stdio, 5 commits (365c78a\u2192c678017): `recall_search` (structured hits + `gap_warning` + actionable `advice` + staleness), `recall_index` (agent writes own memory), `recall_stats` (freshness/count), thin `recall_mcp/service.py` over the engine, lifespan-managed store+embedder, + `examples/self_recall_agent.py` (anti-re-litigation `decide()`). **32 tests pass, ruff clean; verified E2E** (real stdio MCP client listed 3 tools + called recall_stats OK). Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-07-recall-m2-mcp.md`. \u26a0\ufe0f **Built INLINE, not subagent-driven** \u2014 the general-purpose subagents misfired repeatedly (delegation loops: spawned children + waited instead of implementing); switched to inline for reliability.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/project_recall_public_rag_repo_2026-07-06.md",

        "text": "Until 2026-08-15 the recall project had **no MCP servers at all**: no `.mcp.json`, nothing under\n`mcpServers` in `~/.claude.json`. The five internal servers were configured only for\n`progetto sentimental`, so recall sessions never had them. All five were reachable the whole time,\nwhich is why this looked like a working setup and was not.\n\n## They are reachable, and their corpus is not this repo",

The current Codex\nprocess still holds the old closed connections because MCP configuration is read at client start;\nrestart or open a new session in this worktree to load the repaired transports.",

That is the failure mode to watch\nfor: not an error, a wrong corpus.\n\n## What was actually missing: recall did not dogfood itself\n\nrecall ships an MCP server (`recall_mcp`, 10 tools) and `docs/USING_WITH_CLAUDE.md` documents\nexactly how to install it. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-07-recall-m2-mcp.md`. \u26a0\ufe0f **Built INLINE, not subagent-driven** \u2014 the general-purpose subagents misfired repeatedly (delegation loops: spawned children + waited instead of implementing); switched to inline for reliability.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/project_recall_public_rag_repo_2026-07-06.md",

        "text": "Until 2026-08-15 the recall project had **no MCP servers at all**: no `.mcp.json`, nothing under\n`mcpServers` in `~/.claude.json`.   "outcome": "abstained",
  "answer": null,
  "clarification_request": null,
  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "what must happen to a scheduled deadman check when a gate closes early",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,
    "decision_state": "supported",
    "calibrated": true,
    "stale": false,

    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "c93653f255ee2ae29a525591bef4c4fbde14d7b4538c4aff652be10b04631946",
        "text": "funder wallet): `post_exit_7d` is a lower bound, so a low ratio is confounded \u21d2 NEEDS_DATA not a false FAIL. To resolve: build a **post-exit pool reward-RATE source** (gamma per-market rate after exit), else close as NEEDS_DATA.\n- \ud83d\udd11 #1896 and #1897 are deliberately opposed \u2014 cannot both PASS. A PASS re-arms nothing (lane closed #1804, maker halted `_RMK_KILL`).\n\n## 5. \u00a72b deadman checks (local scheduled tasks)\n`gate-check-1895-2026-07-30`, `gate-check-1897-2026-07-30`, `gate-check-1896-2026-08-06` \u2014 each runs the gate-check + posts the verdict (run when the app is open / next launch).",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/project-lrp-gate-work-2026-07-19.md",
        "ordinal": 5,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:32.936348+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5550750659428559,
        "confidence": 0.8730087094952274,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "b1e319607401c01d2645d5614aa5f0cbf541a9dab0967c4b83f5c0d1c62094b2",
        "text": "**Why:** CLAUDE.md \u00a72b makes every gate carry a scheduled check as its deadman, but there is no\ninverse rule. An orphaned deadman is worse than a missing one: it arrives with confident,\nself-contained instructions and no knowledge that the lane died, so the default behaviour is to\nre-run a closed experiment and post numbers that invite a reopen. The scheduled task's own\nframing is stale data, not authority \u2014 [[feedback-verify-collector-terminal-table-2026-07-14]]\nis the same failure shape one layer down.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-closing-a-gate-early-must-cancel-its-scheduled-check-2026-07-21.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:15.866789+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6133376542728443,
        "confidence": 0.9874523175821098,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "87360cf238b9be73104d1ced608462149da32db54da70e47051274df296ecf84",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n1. On arming any probe, note the **terminal table** the gate query reads (e.g. `polymarket_live_orders`, `*_fills`) \u2014 not the signals or dry-ledger table.\n2. Within 24-48h, run `SELECT count(*), max(<ts>) FROM <terminal_table> WHERE <edge_id/slug filter> AND <ts> >= <arm_date>`. Zero rows \u21d2 **not armed** \u2014 fix or close, do not let it ride to the gate date.\n3. Sanity-check the whole `systemd-analyze cat-config` view of the unit, not just the base unit file \u2014 drop-ins (`*.d/*.conf`) override `Environment=`, and a later `EnvironmentFile=` can too ([[reference_systemd_environmentfile_overrides_environment_2026-07-12]]).\n4. Every gate issue must have a paired scheduled check (CLAUDE.md Session-Close \u00a72b). #1594 had none, which is why it drifted 13 days unnoticed.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-verify-collector-terminal-table-2026-07-14.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:18.778721+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5302005288184164,
        "confidence": 0.7082813135554336,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "baa846d2844718d3a3590b39f318bec6071bfd8e1c5c3649e484e5d4abbb0d30",
        "text": "Closing a `gate` issue early (lane death, venue repricing, moot verdict) leaves its paired\n`/schedule` deadman armed. On 2026-07-21 the `maker-net-tuner-gate-run` task fired for gate\n#1494 \u2014 closed 2026-07-16 with the LRP lane. The task instructions still read as a live gate\n(\"ahead of the 2026-07-21 gate\") and prescribed training + posting a learned-vs-baseline\nverdict.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-closing-a-gate-early-must-cancel-its-scheduled-check-2026-07-21.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:15.857847+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6259298288163393,
        "confidence": 0.9925529431724239,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "e3c2c95967af3f2506d9a8d5867adf3d12d68c8a70c1f2d3197cf3308da501b5",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n- Session-Close \u00a72c (gate resolved \u2192 comment + close) is incomplete: also **cancel or repoint\n  the paired scheduled check** in the same session.\n- When a scheduled gate task fires, **read the issue state FIRST**. `state: CLOSED` \u21d2 the correct\n  output is a SUPERSEDED note on the issue, not a run.\n- Do not treat \"the run is technically feasible\" as a reason to run. #1494's substrate was still\n  writing and the tuner still imported cleanly; the blocker was economic (`rewardsMinSize`\n  20\u2192200 priced us out), and no allocator result could move it.\n  See [[project-lrp-reward-farming-closed-venue-repricing-2026-07-16]] and\n  [[feedback-venue-can-reprice-you-out-overnight-2026-07-16]].",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-closing-a-gate-early-must-cancel-its-scheduled-check-2026-07-21.md",
        "ordinal": 2,

        "text": "403)**: il deadman \u00a72b non gira da ~06. Fix = utente (ri-autorizza claude.ai/code). \ud83d\udd11 **una data di gate non prova che un check partir\u00e0.** \u2705 Rimpiazzo: timer VPS3 \u2192 verdetto in TABELLA. [[incident-cloud-routines-all-auto-disabled-repo-access-2026-07-30]]\r\n- \u2705 **#1895 RIAPERTA + deadman shippato \u2014 nessuna decisione fino al 08-13** (`gate-1895-check.timer` VPS3 \u2192 `gate_1895_check_log`). \u26a0\ufe0f i fill pre-15:47Z sono sotto il drain print-only. [[project-gate-1895-touch-needs-data-markout-never-written-2026-07-30]]\r\n- \ud83d\udd34\ud83d\udd34 **#1761 NEEDS_DATA \u2192 09-04, ma la lane BTC 15m NON accumula pi\u00f9**: `updown-lag-racer` \u00e8 `active` e ticchetta con **`enter=0`, `outside_window` 100%** dal 07-31 \u21d2 **zero fill dal 07-23**; estendere non serve finch\u00e9 il fill path \u00e8 rotto. \ud83d\udd34 **APERTA: chi ha messo `notional_usd=15`**",
