    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "4b1dedd73c4c27960431e58ca07ea4fd44487560c6922906a49b54bf328badc8",
        "text": "Before deploying any sudoers lockdown that replaces wildcard `NOPASSWD: ALL` with a Cmnd_Alias allowlist, **verify whether the target user has a password set**. Without one, sudo for any non-allowlisted command silently fails with \"a terminal is required to read the password\" \u2014 the operator is locked out of every ad-hoc admin operation, and even console root login becomes the only recovery path.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:19.437400+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.7183369612198166,
        "confidence": 0.9998429624674172,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "214c59a178ef664b6c20bd76bda001473723cd9034aeab6b53b32c125932d9bb",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n- Step 0 (always): `sudo passwd -S <user>` (or `sudo grep <user>: /etc/shadow | cut -d: -f2`) \u2014 if it shows `L` / `*` / empty hash, no password is set.\n- If no password: ask the operator before deploy, *\"do you want me to set a password first (so non-allowlist commands prompt + work) or accept that the allowlist is a hard wall?\"*. Do not assume.\n- Even when a password exists, double-check the operator can recover via console \u2014 every Cmnd_Alias deploy needs a documented break-glass path that's been tested.\n- Keep the pre-deploy file backup at a path the new sudoers still permits to read (so post-deploy rollback to the prior policy is possible from the same shell). The 2026-05-05 deploy left the backup at `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment.bak.<TS>` \u2014 DENIED to read by the new",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:19.447702+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6555656585434472,
        "confidence": 0.9978334586352453,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "9c620896596e300a7d15f7d0fa88383421d7475d57437b5d89fd251092433b84",
        "text": "**Why:** 2026-05-05 redteam fix session. Saw `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment: sentiment ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL` and assumed \"NOPASSWD\" implied \"no password set\". Deployed Cmnd_Alias lockdown. User immediately hit `[sudo] password for sentiment:` prompts when running outside the allowlist (e.g., `tee /etc/contabo/credentials.env`, `docker compose up -d` for a config refresh). The password actually *was* set, but the user couldn't remember it \u2014 equivalent to no fallback. Recovery options collapsed to (a) Contabo VNC console root login (operator did not have access at that moment) or (b) a destructive snapshot revert (the 2026-05-05 attempt got 400/404 from the Contabo API depending on body shape \u2014 `{}` body returns 404 'Cannot POST', empty body returns 400 'body cannot be empty'). The session",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:19.445146+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6403689575305274,
        "confidence": 0.9959160938943287,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "8146703dfcd38c6c1fd3e38ca2da4c397dcaa57292dfbeba7b7c310bfdcc0800",
        "text": "**Rule:** On VPS (`sentiment@100.91.148.25`), the `sentiment` user **cannot read `.env`** and has a tightly allowlisted sudo. Treat the hardened workflow as mandatory.\n\n**Why:** Big security hardening done 2026-05-10/12. `.env` is now `root:sentiment-secrets 0640`; `sentiment` is NOT in `sentiment-secrets` (only `ftmo`, `chartapi`, `fundr` are). Sudo went from `ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL` \u2192 aliased allowlist in `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment` (`SENTIMENT_SYSTEMCTL/JOURNAL/HEALTHCHECK_WRITE/READ_CONFIG/NETDIAG/AUDIT/DOCKER/PSQL`). Previous workflow muscle memory (`sudo systemctl restart anything`, `cat .env`, `sudo psql`, `daemon-reload`) is broken by design and must not be reintroduced.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_hardened_vps2_secrets_2026-05-12.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:21.534223+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5540552304403555,
        "confidence": 0.8682022433108356,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "312b1e780623cd987a23208d96f3450e5a4379924bdf3c9aaa6a095bb5ccfeb2",
        "text": "`scripts/deploy.sh` does `${SUDO}mkdir -p '$BACKUP_DIR'` (line ~132) and `${SUDO}mkdir -p '$REMOTE_ROOT/$pdir' && ${SUDO}chown ...` (line ~144). On VPS2 with the sentiment user the sudo NOPASSWD allowlist (per `reference_vps2_sudo_allowlist.md`) covers systemctl/journalctl/PG/docker monitoring but **not `mkdir`** or `chown`. Result: deploy aborts with `sudo: a password is required` whenever the target subtree doesn't already exist on VPS2 (new research dir, new module).\n\n**Why:** Allowlist was narrowed in 2026-05-04 hardening pass; deploy.sh was written assuming broader sudo. Verified 2026-05-05 deploying EU phase 0 research files \u2014 failed on `mkdir -p /opt/backups/...` and `mkdir -p /opt/sentiment_agent/research/eu_phase0/`.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_deploy_sh_sudo_mkdir_gap.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:20.612985+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.535438998477491,
        "confidence": 0.7514263921044187,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "d86816edf5e1dc76af6b3a8d3455a3da4177c423263efb4e44b582c4d638dcd4",
        "text": "backup at `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment.bak.<TS>` \u2014 DENIED to read by the new `cat /etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment` allow-pattern (only the exact filename is whitelisted), so even reading the backup required root.\n- Pair sudoers tightening with a snapshot taken *and tested for revert* (Contabo `revert` endpoint requires the right body shape \u2014 empty `{}` returns 400, omitted body works for at least some snapshot states; verify before relying on it).\n\nAvoid the original mistake: never deploy a hard sudo lockdown without first confirming both (a) password fallback exists and (b) console recovery is reachable.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:19.455417+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6391986799001304,
        "confidence": 0.9957120250842878,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "a861b515d434b99f856d2b55cbb246dc2effd35d98652ccedac162c32f34239c",
        "text": "alerting in the same commit).\n- Live VPS3 `/etc/sudoers.d/` diverges from repo `security/sudoers.d/`: the box uses tight **per-unit** `systemctl restart <exact-unit>` grants (`91-copytrade-watchdog`, now `91-shadow-maker-recorder-watchdog`), NOT the repo's staged broad `restart *`. Mirror the per-unit pattern; never deploy the broad file.\n\nRelated: [[feedback-verify-collector-terminal-table-2026-07-14]] (phantom-gate / verify the terminal table) \u00b7 [[project_fast_maker_m1_speed_test_2026-07-09]] (engine_ws spine).\n\n---\n\n**ROOT CAUSE FOUND & FIXED (2026-07-15, master 810bb51e) \u2014 the watchdog was the safety net; THIS is the real bug.**",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/incident-shadow-maker-recorder-watchdog-autorestart-2026-07-15.md",
        "ordinal": 5,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:27.525452+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5648397375595494,
        "confidence": 0.9118463907977279,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "4fa3aa67f6b37385eaa9b43554c53eaaa7beefb5c89bf322966b84460bbe5637",
        "text": "## NON coperti (richiedono password sudo, NON eseguire autonomamente)\n\n- `apt`, `apt-get`, `apt install|update|upgrade|autoremove|clean` \u2014 install/cleanup pacchetti\n- `tee` verso path arbitrari (es. `/etc/sysctl.d/`, `/etc/logrotate.d/`) \u2014 solo `/etc/sentiment/healthcheck.url` \u00e8 coperto\n- `sysctl --system`, `sysctl -w` \u2014 tweak kernel\n- `tuned-adm profile *` \u2014 performance tuning\n- `logrotate` (esecuzione + config write)\n- `usermod`, `gpasswd`, `passwd root` \u2014 esplicitamente `!` (negate, mai concessi)\n- `visudo` \u2014 esplicitamente `!` negate\n- `cat /root/age/*` e variants \u2014 esplicitamente `!` (age key protection)\n- `docker` per container fuori dal set monitoring (no general `docker exec`, `docker run`, `docker build`)\n\n## Implicazioni operative",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference_vps2_sudo_allowlist.md",

        "text": "Before deploying any sudoers lockdown that replaces wildcard `NOPASSWD: ALL` with a Cmnd_Alias allowlist, **verify whether the target user has a password set**. Without one, sudo for any non-allowlisted command silently fails with \"a terminal is required to read the password\" \u2014 the operator is locked out of every ad-hoc admin operation, and even console root login becomes the only recovery path.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",

      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "214c59a178ef664b6c20bd76bda001473723cd9034aeab6b53b32c125932d9bb",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n- Step 0 (always): `sudo passwd -S <user>` (or `sudo grep <user>: /etc/shadow | cut -d: -f2`) \u2014 if it shows `L` / `*` / empty hash, no password is set.\n- If no password: ask the operator before deploy, *\"do you want me to set a password first (so non-allowlist commands prompt + work) or accept that the allowlist is a hard wall?\"*. Do not assume.\n- Even when a password exists, double-check the operator can recover via console \u2014 every Cmnd_Alias deploy needs a documented break-glass path that's been tested.\n- Keep the pre-deploy file backup at a path the new sudoers still permits to read (so post-deploy rollback to the prior policy is possible from the same shell). The 2026-05-05 deploy left the backup at `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment.bak.<TS>` \u2014 DENIED to read by the new",

        "text": "**Why:** 2026-05-05 redteam fix session. Saw `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment: sentiment ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL` and assumed \"NOPASSWD\" implied \"no password set\". Deployed Cmnd_Alias lockdown. User immediately hit `[sudo] password for sentiment:` prompts when running outside the allowlist (e.g., `tee /etc/contabo/credentials.env`, `docker compose up -d` for a config refresh). The password actually *was* set, but the user couldn't remember it \u2014 equivalent to no fallback. Recovery options collapsed to (a) Contabo VNC console root login (operator did not have access at that moment) or (b) a destructive snapshot revert (the 2026-05-05 attempt got 400/404 from the Contabo API depending on body shape \u2014 `{}` body returns 404 'Cannot POST', empty body returns 400 'body cannot be empty'). Treat the hardened workflow as mandatory.\n\n**Why:** Big security hardening done 2026-05-10/12. `.env` is now `root:sentiment-secrets 0640`; `sentiment` is NOT in `sentiment-secrets` (only `ftmo`, `chartapi`, `fundr` are). Previous workflow muscle memory (`sudo systemctl restart anything`, `cat .env`, `sudo psql`, `daemon-reload`) is broken by design and must not be reintroduced.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_hardened_vps2_secrets_2026-05-12.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:21.534223+00:00",

        "text": "`scripts/deploy.sh` does `${SUDO}mkdir -p '$BACKUP_DIR'` (line ~132) and `${SUDO}mkdir -p '$REMOTE_ROOT/$pdir' && ${SUDO}chown ...` (line ~144). On VPS2 with the sentiment user the sudo NOPASSWD allowlist (per `reference_vps2_sudo_allowlist.md`) covers systemctl/journalctl/PG/docker monitoring but **not `mkdir`** or `chown`. Verified 2026-05-05 deploying EU phase 0 research files \u2014 failed on `mkdir -p /opt/backups/...` and `mkdir -p /opt/sentiment_agent/research/eu_phase0/`.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_deploy_sh_sudo_mkdir_gap.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:20.612985+00:00",

        "text": "backup at `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment.bak.<TS>` \u2014 DENIED to read by the new `cat /etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment` allow-pattern (only the exact filename is whitelisted), so even reading the backup required root.\n- Pair sudoers tightening with a snapshot taken *and tested for revert* (Contabo `revert` endpoint requires the right body shape \u2014 empty `{}` returns 400, omitted body works for at least some snapshot states; verify before relying on it).\n\nAvoid the original mistake: never deploy a hard sudo lockdown without first confirming both (a) password fallback exists and (b) console recovery is reachable.",

Every one passed on isolated re-run.\nBudget for it: the full suite is 15-20 minutes, so a false red is expensive to chase.\n\n## 2026-08-15: the root cause is fixed in the repo. Use the scripts.\n\n`tests/conftest.py` no longer defaults to `localhost:5432`. Unset, `TEST_DSN` points at port 1,\nso an unconfigured run skips loudly instead of silently sharing a database. The manual `docker\nrun` recipe below is now `scripts/session-db.sh`:",

An untouched file errored identically, which is how\nI knew it was not my change. `_db_available()` only skips the bootstrap when the DSN is\n*unreachable*, so the fix was to make it unreachable:\n\nRECALL_TEST_DSN=\"postgresql://nobody:nobody@127.0.0.1:1/none\" python -m pytest tests/<one_file>.py -q",

    "query": "why does the test suite have no default database DSN",
    "decision": "answer",

    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "db6f1a502896606f032ba034bd0c8a9b4a0593c566efcc09156d92d5104e80a1",
        "text": "RE-call's DB-backed suite produces failures that have nothing to do with the code under test,\nrepeatedly and at wildly different scales: 15 failed + 5 errors, 473 errors, 41 failed + 59\nerrors, 8 failed + 12 errors, and single one-off errors. Every one passed on isolated re-run.\nBudget for it: the full suite is 15-20 minutes, so a false red is expensive to chase.\n\n## 2026-08-15: the root cause is fixed in the repo. Use the scripts.\n\n`tests/conftest.py` no longer defaults to `localhost:5432`. Unset, `TEST_DSN` points at port 1,\nso an unconfigured run skips loudly instead of silently sharing a database. The manual `docker\nrun` recipe below is now `scripts/session-db.sh`:",
        "source": "recall/concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.805387+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5624512098758702,
        "confidence": 0.9034755144151164,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "24cf920cc2704acd44d739e1d0fdacfb4911ab4967287ff0e7dc2fd6239a972e",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f **The exception, and only this one: a single DB-free FILE.** 2026-08-15 a reachable but\nschema-incompatible database made `conftest.py`'s session-scoped autouse\n`_bootstrap_default_test_schema` raise out of `apply_migrations`, which **ERRORed every test in the\nrepo**, including files that touch no database. An untouched file errored identically, which is how\nI knew it was not my change. `_db_available()` only skips the bootstrap when the DSN is\n*unreachable*, so the fix was to make it unreachable:\n\nRECALL_TEST_DSN=\"postgresql://nobody:nobody@127.0.0.1:1/none\" python -m pytest tests/<one_file>.py -q",
        "source": "recall/concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",
        "ordinal": 8,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.811393+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5623640343708951,
        "confidence": 0.9031569556308944,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "98a2fd0ce14fd81715161654a24b0c29caca9c76c988e34eb5209a626d3d89a3",
        "text": "Con un DB usa-e-getta (`recall_pytest`, owner `recall_beam`, pgvector 0.8.2): **1429 passed,\n1 failed, 4 skipped**. Runner riusabile: `/opt/recall-fb/run_db_tests.py` \u2014 legge il DSN da\n`/opt/recall-beam/.env`, sostituisce **solo** il nome del DB, blocca `recall_bench`/\n`sentiment_agent`/`postgres`, toglie `RECALL_DSN`, non mette mai la password su una command\nline. \u26a0\ufe0f la suite stessa rifiuta di partire se `RECALL_TEST_DSN == RECALL_DSN` (\u00abthese tests\nDROP TABLES\u00bb).",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference-recall-checkouts-vps2-pinned-2026-07-29.md",
        "ordinal": 11,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:06:22.671367+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5354442277285927,
        "confidence": 0.7514672578252526,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "83e62ed61daead12e9e9a1ddf9f7e764db0537dd0e4819d94db8d36dcd1594e0",
        "text": "\u26d4 **Never \"isolate\" a DB-free change by pointing the DSN at a dead port.** `_db_available()`\ncovers most of the suite but not all: three `tests/test_bench_systems.py::test_recall_system_*`\ntests FAIL with `psycopg.errors.ConnectionTimeout` instead of skipping, manufacturing a red that\nlooks like your change.",
        "source": "recall/concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",

        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.810655+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,

        "text": "Two pytest sessions running at the same time against the same test database collide. `tests/conftest.py`\ncalls `apply_migrations` from a session fixture, and `recall.schema`'s guard refuses the second one:\n\nrecall.schema.ConcurrentMigrator: another RE-call schema migrator is already running\n\nThe loser does not fail one test. **Every** test errors at setup, so the run reports e.g.\n`3 skipped, 62 errors` with no failures at all.         "chunk_id": "8de55c1fd87dbd4e48952d91019be0b4f35ed3ccb3fc0041eb9b4434265deff6",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n1. A suite verdict is the SUMMARY LINE, never an exit code. An output file with no pytest output\n   means \"did not run or was lost\", whatever the code says.\n2. Before relaunching anything DB-backed, list live python processes and match COMMAND LINES:\n   two suites on one session database invalidate each other silently.\n4. Distinguish your processes from other sessions' by command line before killing: this machine\n   routinely runs parallel sessions with their own suites.",
        "source": "recall/background-suite-exit-0-with-empty-output-is-not-green.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:35.541082+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5672482429894976,
        "confidence": 0.9196177695693883,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "aefa693b11a3901015aa3bd3ffff724f6f3170bb54c08ccb75418c9ad377506f",
        "text": "| Symptom | Cause |\n| --- | --- |\n| `ConcurrentMigrator` in fixture setup | two pytest processes contend for the schema-migration advisory lock; `scripts/ablate_store_latency_guards.py` documents it |\n| `LockNotAvailable: canceling statement due to lock timeout` | another session on the SAME container, still running |\n| `test_rate_limit_http.py`, `test_mcp_auth_http.py` | these stand up real HTTP servers and contend on PORTS; a private container does not protect them |\n| `FileNotFoundError` inside `tmp_path` | pytest keeps only the 3 most recent `pytest-of-<user>/pytest-<n>` roots and prunes older ones AT STARTUP, so a new run deletes the dirs of runs in flight |\n| pool / latency / backend-count assertions (\"pool churned: 3 distinct backends\u2026\") | CPU contention, not DB contention |\n|",
        "source": "recall/concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",
        "ordinal": 14,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.824048+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.537134674958309,
        "confidence": 0.7644409311672008,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "639814e935a0470b83ab54288e94db52693a71cf4f61d955bfb2cfd87701cf45",
        "text": "**Why it matters:** the guard is working as designed, but its failure signature looks exactly like a\ncatastrophic breakage of the code under test. It cost me a wrong conclusion once: in a mutation-testing\nharness I counted two mutants as \"caught\" because the suite went red, when the redness was this\ncollision and not the mutant.\n\n**How to apply:** run pytest sessions in this repo **sequentially**, never overlapping. In any harness\nthat shells out to pytest in a loop, treat `errors` and `failed` as different evidence: only `failed`\nmeans a test caught something. Retry (or abort) on seeing `ConcurrentMigrator` in the output rather\nthan scoring that run. See also [[bench-systems-suite-spends-openrouter-credits]] for the other trap in\nthis same file.\n\n---",
        "source": "recall/pytest-sessions-cannot-run-in-parallel.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:49.847457+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5553669929504434,
        "confidence": 0.8743567076816612,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "874f8bb956559895a95fd86e0116c1ec288ab01b260837b2786c93e76f3fb623",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **The competing process is usually one I started myself.** A `bug-auditor` subagent runs pytest.\nChaining `pytest A && pytest B` overlaps if the first has not fully released its connections. Both\nhappened repeatedly, and I diagnosed the results as broken apparatus, code regression, catalog\nbloat and machine contention before noticing I was the other party. **Tell subagents explicitly not\nto touch the database, and never run a suite while one is live.**\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **The failing test set CHANGES every run** and each one passes in isolation, which reads exactly\nlike order-dependent shared state. There is no randomiser installed \u2014 it is whichever test happened\nto be migrating when the lock was taken.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference-concurrentmigrator-false-failures-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:06:21.234026+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5886054214419616,
        "confidence": 0.9654694750487122,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "2b011a564c4d7bee666544b762d0917291aed1bfe43c6f1ac2c7091fb440dfd9",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f **CI is the arbiter, not this box.** The GitHub runner gets a private database and no competing\nsession; both PRs (#234, #239) went green there on `test` while the local suite still showed\ncollisions. 12 worktrees share this clone \u2192 [[feedback-concurrent-sessions-race-the-same-clone-2026-07-24]].\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **Write the expected pass count BEFORE the run.** \"3115 passed, 0 failed\" reads as success; only\na committed prediction of 3117 made the gap visible, and that gap is what led to this diagnosis.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference-concurrentmigrator-false-failures-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:06:21.242329+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.569634846492428,
        "confidence": 0.9266968471749202,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "0bfb5da020a86a1fb214a049ef3d78014751751687f46028ac89633e6ef4efed",
        "text": "**Moved here 2026-08-15** from the `RE-call` memory store, which forked from this one when the\ndirectory was renamed to `recall`. It sat there unreachable for ten days while I worked the same\nfailure family from the other store. Renaming a project directory silently forks its memory.\n\nThe collision is narrower now but not gone: `scripts/session-db.sh up` gives each checkout its own\ndatabase, so two sessions in *different* checkouts no longer contend for one migrator. Two runs in\nthe *same* checkout still do, because they share a DSN. The reading rule survives intact and is the\ndurable part: **`errors` and `failed` are different evidence, and only `failed` means a test caught\nsomething.** See [[concurrent-pytest-false-reds]].",

        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5573831464419884,
        "confidence": 0.8833351541294734,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      }

        "text": "Two pytest sessions running at the same time against the same test database collide. `tests/conftest.py`\ncalls `apply_migrations` from a session fixture, and `recall.schema`'s guard refuses the second one:\n\nrecall.schema.ConcurrentMigrator: another RE-call schema migrator is already running\n\nThe loser does not fail one test. **Every** test errors at setup, so the run reports e.g.\n`3 skipped, 62 errors` with no failures at all. Reproduced deliberately on 2026-08-05 with three\nconcurrent runs of `tests/test_bench_systems.py`: one passed, two errored wholesale.",
        "source": "recall/pytest-sessions-cannot-run-in-parallel.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:49.845452+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5924287085277622,
        "confidence": 0.9704231697997363,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "8de55c1fd87dbd4e48952d91019be0b4f35ed3ccb3fc0041eb9b4434265deff6",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n1. A suite verdict is the SUMMARY LINE, never an exit code. An output file with no pytest output\n   means \"did not run or was lost\", whatever the code says.\n2. Launch long suites detached with their own log (`nohup python -u -m pytest tests/ -q > log\n   2>&1 &`, the `-u` matters or the log stays empty for minutes) and watch the log with a\n   Monitor until-loop for the summary line.\n3. Before relaunching anything DB-backed, list live python processes and match COMMAND LINES:\n   two suites on one session database invalidate each other silently.\n4. Distinguish your processes from other sessions' by command line before killing: this machine\n   routinely runs parallel sessions with their own suites.",
        "source": "recall/background-suite-exit-0-with-empty-output-is-not-green.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:35.541082+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5672482429894976,
        "confidence": 0.9196177695693883,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "aefa693b11a3901015aa3bd3ffff724f6f3170bb54c08ccb75418c9ad377506f",
        "text": "| Symptom | Cause |\n| --- | --- |\n| `ConcurrentMigrator` in fixture setup | two pytest processes contend for the schema-migration advisory lock; `scripts/ablate_store_latency_guards.py` documents it |\n| `LockNotAvailable: canceling statement due to lock timeout` | another session on the SAME container, still running |\n| `test_rate_limit_http.py`, `test_mcp_auth_http.py` | these stand up real HTTP servers and contend on PORTS; a private container does not protect them |\n| `FileNotFoundError` inside `tmp_path` | pytest keeps only the 3 most recent `pytest-of-<user>/pytest-<n>` roots and prunes older ones AT STARTUP, so a new run deletes the dirs of runs in flight |\n| pool / latency / backend-count assertions (\"pool churned: 3 distinct backends\u2026\") | CPU contention, not DB contention |\n|",
        "source": "recall/concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",
        "ordinal": 14,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.824048+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.537134674958309,
        "confidence": 0.7644409311672008,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "639814e935a0470b83ab54288e94db52693a71cf4f61d955bfb2cfd87701cf45",
        "text": "**Why it matters:** the guard is working as designed, but its failure signature looks exactly like a\ncatastrophic breakage of the code under test. It cost me a wrong conclusion once: in a mutation-testing\nharness I counted two mutants as \"caught\" because the suite went red, when the redness was this\ncollision and not the mutant.\n\n**How to apply:** run pytest sessions in this repo **sequentially**, never overlapping. In any harness\nthat shells out to pytest in a loop, treat `errors` and `failed` as different evidence: only `failed`\nmeans a test caught something. Retry (or abort) on seeing `ConcurrentMigrator` in the output rather\nthan scoring that run. See also [[bench-systems-suite-spends-openrouter-credits]] for the other trap in\nthis same file.\n\n---",
        "source": "recall/pytest-sessions-cannot-run-in-parallel.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:49.847457+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5553669929504434,
        "confidence": 0.8743567076816612,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "874f8bb956559895a95fd86e0116c1ec288ab01b260837b2786c93e76f3fb623",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **The competing process is usually one I started myself.** A `bug-auditor` subagent runs pytest.\nChaining `pytest A && pytest B` overlaps if the first has not fully released its connections. Both\nhappened repeatedly, and I diagnosed the results as broken apparatus, code regression, catalog\nbloat and machine contention before noticing I was the other party. **Tell subagents explicitly not\nto touch the database, and never run a suite while one is live.**\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **The failing test set CHANGES every run** and each one passes in isolation, which reads exactly\nlike order-dependent shared state. There is no randomiser installed \u2014 it is whichever test happened\nto be migrating when the lock was taken.",

rows.payload:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "outcome": "abstained",
  "answer": null,
  "clarification_request": null,
  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "how long does the full test suite take with a database",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,
    "decision_state": "supported",
    "calibrated": true,
    "stale": false,
    "embedding_profile": "voyage:voyage-4",
    "retrieval_profile": "fast",

    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "f8005f74b62dde24c84e11613a32d461cdedceb6d399ef63479cece580831dfa",
        "text": "**Measured 2026-08-18** on this Windows workstation, with a session container:\n\n```\n5694 passed, 32 skipped in 1857.08s (0:30:57)\n```\n\n`CLAUDE.md:140` states \"The full suite takes about **12 minutes** with a database and about 5\nwithout.\" That is **stale by a factor of two and a half**, and it is a claim in a file loaded into\nevery session, so it is believed by default.\n\n## Why it matters beyond the number\n\nA 15 or 20 minute timeout looks generous against the documented figure and **kills the run at\nroughly two thirds**. That is exactly what happened here on the first attempt, and the killed run\nthen reported success because its exit code came from a `| tail` rather than from pytest. Two\nindependent defects lined up to turn \"the suite did not finish\" into \"the suite passed\".",
        "source": "recall/full-suite-takes-31-minutes-not-12.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:41.563034+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6604924201965332,
        "confidence": 0.9982363331701865,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "db6f1a502896606f032ba034bd0c8a9b4a0593c566efcc09156d92d5104e80a1",
        "text": "RE-call's DB-backed suite produces failures that have nothing to do with the code under test,\nrepeatedly and at wildly different scales: 15 failed + 5 errors, 473 errors, 41 failed + 59\nerrors, 8 failed + 12 errors, and single one-off errors. Every one passed on isolated re-run.\nBudget for it: the full suite is 15-20 minutes, so a false red is expensive to chase.\n\n## 2026-08-15: the root cause is fixed in the repo. Use the scripts.\n\n`tests/conftest.py` no longer defaults to `localhost:5432`. Unset, `TEST_DSN` points at port 1,\nso an unconfigured run skips loudly instead of silently sharing a database. The manual `docker\nrun` recipe below is now `scripts/session-db.sh`:",
        "source": "recall/concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.805387+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5312032699584961,
        "confidence": 0.7168738064792394,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "0c77c608de27674243021a843f506f14ea12e39aba75a6fb35c017dacd10e4c2",
        "text": "\u2014 read before adding any guard keyed on database privilege. `docker-compose.yml` and CI both hand the suite a superuser, so an RLS guard broke 9 HTTP-server tests; `conftest.unprivileged_dsn` already exists for it.\n- [Fastembed is not why the suite is slow](fastembed-is-not-why-the-suite-is-slow.md) \u2014 measured 2026-08-26: all real-model tests are 73 tests / 80s; >40 min runs mean serial or a loaded box, and make test now preflights via scripts/suite-preflight.sh.\n- [agent-memory-bench site: live](agent-memory-bench-site-2026-08-26.md) \u2014 read BEFORE editing any page there: the public site names NO third-party product and a test enforces it, while the harness still runs all eight arms under their real names. Deployed at giulioder.github.io/agent-memory-bench; leaderboard.js is generated",
        "source": "recall/project_index.md",
        "ordinal": 55,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:48.808997+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5943018375129058,
        "confidence": 0.9725915950618881,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "b3312334639692b044df0ae796484e9f6de1e30fc8cef3be4ee5d22947b875f4",
        "text": "Measured 2026-08-21 on PR #452. Locally: **6279 passed, 34 skipped, ruff clean**, full suite against\na real database, 36 minutes. On CI: **4 checks red**. Nothing was flaky; every failure was real and\nevery one was mine.",
        "source": "recall/a-green-local-suite-hid-four-ci-gates.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:29.696498+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6533231735229492,
        "confidence": 0.9976208416784456,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "4c9f22d4cc5874e274afca801badefa2fae02298cb72150da3e7e90573edcbed",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f **The same suite on the same machine varied by twenty minutes.** Budget for the top of the\nrange, not the middle, and never set a timeout from a previous run's number. The test count grew\nfrom 5694 to ~6500 over four days, so part of this is real growth and part is load: the 54 minute\nrun overlapped other work on the box.\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **34 skips is the healthy figure now**, up from 32. Read the skip count before calling a run\ngreen; several hundred means the DB tests never ran.",
        "source": "recall/full-suite-takes-31-minutes-not-12.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:41.530663+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.638900101184845,
        "confidence": 0.9956583541530496,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "78b449766a2975f459c179a66cf6c675648823fbddcad1b3287d2002da510960",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **Read the SKIP COUNT, not only the pass count.** 32 is healthy here; `CLAUDE.md` says roughly 22\nand warns that several hundred means the DB tests never ran and the reason is printed in the skip\ntext.\n\n## Re-measure\n\n```bash\neval \"$(scripts/session-db.sh up)\" && export RECALL_TEST_DSN\npython -m pytest tests/ -q --timeout=300 > /tmp/fullsuite.log 2>&1; echo \"EXIT: $?\"\ntail -3 /tmp/fullsuite.log\nscripts/session-db.sh down\n```\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f **Redirect, never pipe**, if you intend to read the exit code: a pipeline reports the LAST\ncommand's status. And allow at least 40 minutes.\n\n\u26d4 **Not yet corrected in the repository.** `CLAUDE.md:140` still says 12 minutes; fixing it is a\none line pull request nobody has opened. Until then this memo is the accurate number.",

        "text": "**Measured 2026-08-18** on this Windows workstation, with a session container:\n\n```\n5694 passed, 32 skipped in 1857.08s (0:30:57)\n```\n\n`CLAUDE.md:140` states \"The full suite takes about **12 minutes** with a database and about 5\nwithout.\" That is **stale by a factor of two and a half**, and it is a claim in a file loaded into\nevery session, so it is believed by default.\n\n## Why it matters beyond the number\n\nA 15 or 20 minute timeout looks generous against the documented figure and **kills the run at\nroughly two thirds**.         "ordinal": 0,

        "text": "RE-call's DB-backed suite produces failures that have nothing to do with the code under test,\nrepeatedly and at wildly different scales: 15 failed + 5 errors, 473 errors, 41 failed + 59\nerrors, 8 failed + 12 errors, and single one-off errors. Every one passed on isolated re-run.\nBudget for it: the full suite is 15-20 minutes, so a false red is expensive to chase.\n\n## 2026-08-15: the root cause is fixed in the repo. Use the scripts.\n\n`tests/conftest.py` no longer defaults to `localhost:5432`. Unset, `TEST_DSN` points at port 1,\nso an unconfigured run skips loudly instead of silently sharing a database. The manual `docker\nrun` recipe below is now `scripts/session-db.sh`:",
        "source": "recall/concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.805387+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5312032699584961,
        "confidence": 0.7168738064792394,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },

        "chunk_id": "0c77c608de27674243021a843f506f14ea12e39aba75a6fb35c017dacd10e4c2",
        "text": "\u2014 read before adding any guard keyed on database privilege. `docker-compose.yml` and CI both hand the suite a superuser, so an RLS guard broke 9 HTTP-server tests; `conftest.unprivileged_dsn` already exists for it.\n- [Fastembed is not why the suite is slow](fastembed-is-not-why-the-suite-is-slow.md) \u2014 measured 2026-08-26: all real-model tests are 73 tests / 80s; >40 min runs mean serial or a loaded box, and make test now preflights via scripts/suite-preflight.sh.\n- [agent-memory-bench site: live](agent-memory-bench-site-2026-08-26.md) \u2014 read BEFORE editing any page there: the public site names NO third-party product and a test enforces it, while the harness still runs all eight arms under their real names.         "text": "Measured 2026-08-21 on PR #452. Locally: **6279 passed, 34 skipped, ruff clean**, full suite against\na real database, 36 minutes. On CI: **4 checks red**. Nothing was flaky; every failure was real and\nevery one was mine.",

        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **Read the SKIP COUNT, not only the pass count.** 32 is healthy here; `CLAUDE.md` says roughly 22\nand warns that several hundred means the DB tests never ran and the reason is printed in the skip\ntext.\n\n## Re-measure\n\n```bash\neval \"$(scripts/session-db.sh up)\" && export RECALL_TEST_DSN\npython -m pytest tests/ -q --timeout=300 > /tmp/fullsuite.log 2>&1; echo \"EXIT: $?\"\ntail -3 /tmp/fullsuite.log\nscripts/session-db.sh down\n```\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f **Redirect, never pipe**, if you intend to read the exit code: a pipeline reports the LAST\ncommand's status.         "text": "**Measured 2026-08-18** on this Windows workstation, with a session container:\n\n```\n5694 passed, 32 skipped in 1857.08s (0:30:57)\n```\n\n`CLAUDE.md:140` states \"The full suite takes about **12 minutes** with a database and about 5\nwithout.\" That is **stale by a factor of two and a half**, and it is a claim in a file loaded into\nevery session, so it is believed by default.\n\n## Why it matters beyond the number\n\nA 15 or 20 minute timeout looks generous against the documented figure and **kills the run at\nroughly two thirds**. That is exactly what happened here on the first attempt, and the killed run\nthen reported success because its exit code came from a `| tail` rather than from pytest. Two\nindependent defects lined up to turn \"the suite did not finish\" into \"the suite passed\".",
        "source": "recall/full-suite-takes-31-minutes-not-12.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:41.563034+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6604924201965332,
        "confidence": 0.9982363331701865,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "db6f1a502896606f032ba034bd0c8a9b4a0593c566efcc09156d92d5104e80a1",
        "text": "RE-call's DB-backed suite produces failures that have nothing to do with the code under test,\nrepeatedly and at wildly different scales: 15 failed + 5 errors, 473 errors, 41 failed + 59\nerrors, 8 failed + 12 errors, and single one-off errors. Every one passed on isolated re-run.\nBudget for it: the full suite is 15-20 minutes, so a false red is expensive to chase.\n\n## 2026-08-15: the root cause is fixed in the repo. Use the scripts.\n\n`tests/conftest.py` no longer defaults to `localhost:5432`. Unset, `TEST_DSN` points at port 1,\nso an unconfigured run skips loudly instead of silently sharing a database. The manual `docker\nrun` recipe below is now `scripts/session-db.sh`:",
        "source": "recall/concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.805387+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5312032699584961,
        "confidence": 0.7168738064792394,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "0c77c608de27674243021a843f506f14ea12e39aba75a6fb35c017dacd10e4c2",
        "text": "\u2014 read before adding any guard keyed on database privilege. `docker-compose.yml` and CI both hand the suite a superuser, so an RLS guard broke 9 HTTP-server tests; `conftest.unprivileged_dsn` already exists for it.\n- [Fastembed is not why the suite is slow](fastembed-is-not-why-the-suite-is-slow.md) \u2014 measured 2026-08-26: all real-model tests are 73 tests / 80s; >40 min runs mean serial or a loaded box, and make test now preflights via scripts/suite-preflight.sh.\n- [agent-memory-bench site: live](agent-memory-bench-site-2026-08-26.md) \u2014 read BEFORE editing any page there: the public site names NO third-party product and a test enforces it, while the harness still runs all eight arms under their real names. Deployed at giulioder.github.io/agent-memory-bench; leaderboard.js is generated",
        "source": "recall/project_index.md",
        "ordinal": 55,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:48.808997+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5943018375129058,
        "confidence": 0.9725915950618881,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "b3312334639692b044df0ae796484e9f6de1e30fc8cef3be4ee5d22947b875f4",
        "text": "Measured 2026-08-21 on PR #452. Locally: **6279 passed, 34 skipped, ruff clean**, full suite against\na real database, 36 minutes. On CI: **4 checks red**. Nothing was flaky; every failure was real and\nevery one was mine.",
        "source": "recall/a-green-local-suite-hid-four-ci-gates.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:29.696498+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6533231735229492,
        "confidence": 0.9976208416784456,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "4c9f22d4cc5874e274afca801badefa2fae02298cb72150da3e7e90573edcbed",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f **The same suite on the same machine varied by twenty minutes.** Budget for the top of the\nrange, not the middle, and never set a timeout from a previous run's number. The test count grew\nfrom 5694 to ~6500 over four days, so part of this is real growth and part is load: the 54 minute\nrun overlapped other work on the box.\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **34 skips is the healthy figure now**, up from 32. Read the skip count before calling a run\ngreen; several hundred means the DB tests never ran.",
        "source": "recall/full-suite-takes-31-minutes-not-12.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:41.530663+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.638900101184845,
        "confidence": 0.9956583541530496,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "78b449766a2975f459c179a66cf6c675648823fbddcad1b3287d2002da510960",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **Read the SKIP COUNT, not only the pass count.** 32 is healthy here; `CLAUDE.md` says roughly 22\nand warns that several hundred means the DB tests never ran and the reason is printed in the skip\ntext.\n\n## Re-measure\n\n```bash\neval \"$(scripts/session-db.sh up)\" && export RECALL_TEST_DSN\npython -m pytest tests/ -q --timeout=300 > /tmp/fullsuite.log 2>&1; echo \"EXIT: $?\"\ntail -3 /tmp/fullsuite.log\nscripts/session-db.sh down\n```\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f **Redirect, never pipe**, if you intend to read the exit code: a pipeline reports the LAST\ncommand's status. And allow at least 40 minutes.\n\n\u26d4 **Not yet corrected in the repository.** `CLAUDE.md:140` still says 12 minutes; fixing it is a\none line pull request nobody has opened. Until then this memo is the accurate number.",

        "text": "**Measured 2026-08-18** on this Windows workstation, with a session container:\n\n```\n5694 passed, 32 skipped in 1857.08s (0:30:57)\n```\n\n`CLAUDE.md:140` states \"The full suite takes about **12 minutes** with a database and about 5\nwithout.\" That is **stale by a factor of two and a half**, and it is a claim in a file loaded into\nevery session, so it is believed by default.\n\n## Why it matters beyond the number\n\nA 15 or 20 minute timeout looks generous against the documented figure and **kills the run at\nroughly two thirds**. That is exactly what happened here on the first attempt, and the killed run\nthen reported success because its exit code came from a `| tail` rather than from pytest. Two\nindependent defects lined up to turn \"the suite did not finish\" into \"the suite passed\".",

Every one passed on isolated re-run.\nBudget for it: the full suite is 15-20 minutes, so a false red is expensive to chase.\n\n## 2026-08-15: the root cause is fixed in the repo. Use the scripts.\n\n`tests/conftest.py` no longer defaults to `localhost:5432`. Unset, `TEST_DSN` points at port 1,\nso an unconfigured run skips loudly instead of silently sharing a database. The manual `docker\nrun` recipe below is now `scripts/session-db.sh`:",

The test count grew\nfrom 5694 to ~6500 over four days, so part of this is real growth and part is load: the 54 minute\nrun overlapped other work on the box.\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **34 skips is the healthy figure now**, up from 32. query.query: what happens if I mix two embedding models in one tenant

rows.payload:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "outcome": "abstained",
  "answer": null,
  "clarification_request": null,
  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "what happens if I mix two embedding models in one tenant",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,
    "decision_state": "supported",
    "calibrated": true,
    "stale": false,
    "embedding_profile": "voyage:voyage-4",
    "retrieval_profile": "fast",
    "index_generation": "legacy",
    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "f2440fbf349851c02d440bcfe19c1379d678a2bd43d2fe118b0a28ef7c847afc",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **One embedding model per tenant.** Not a convention: it is the only thing standing between a\nmixed corpus and silently wrong retrieval. When a corpus wants a code model and a prose model,\nthat is two tenants, not one with two writers.\n\nFound on 2026-08-15 designing the `recall_repos` corpus on VPS2 (five repositories, code via\n`voyage-code-3`, docs via `voyage-4`). Ten tenants, `<repo>-code` and `<repo>-docs`, for exactly\nthis reason. The index driver asserts `code_embedder.dim == docs_embedder.dim` before writing,\nbecause both tenants share one table and one fixed vector width.\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f The same reasoning applies to the CHUNKER, but the failure is different and worse: see\n[[chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint]]. Related: [[guards-that-cannot-fail]],\n[[recall-corpus-name-boundary]].",
        "source": "recall/mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:45.166042+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6652348837116442,
        "confidence": 0.9985533028779916,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "ad407afb81ffbe3dd2ee8c1e07aded4d624969c80597ee525aca96a496c33bb3",
        "text": "`RetrievalDiagnostics.embedding_profile` (`recall/retriever.py:325`, `:471`) is **reported, never\nenforced**. Nothing in `recall/store.py` filters rows by it: the only occurrence is a `count(*)\nFILTER (WHERE NOT metadata ? 'embedding_profile')` used for a readiness report. So a tenant holding\npassages from two models is not an error state the code can see.\n\nIt is also not a *loud* failure, which is the part that matters. pgvector would reject a dimension\nmismatch, so two models of DIFFERENT width fail fast. The dangerous case is two models of the\n**same** width: `voyage-4` and `voyage-code-3` are both 1024, so a query embedded with one is\ncosine-compared against passages embedded with the other, the SQL succeeds, and the ranking is\ngarbage that looks exactly like a ranking.",
        "source": "recall/mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:45.160230+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.613179523145549,
        "confidence": 0.9873700742945989,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "1bd4ead73b5ee728600f60c0ee6ba3fccfcd5296b5083ab003b1fc865cc9ac61",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **Verify an embedder by `vector_dims(embedding)`, never by the profile label**: at least on\nthe fastembed path. Extends [[mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent]]: the field that was\nsupposed to make mixing detectable is itself inert, so that lesson is stronger than written.\n\nNot filed as a fix yet. The fix is to derive the default `profile_id` from model name plus\ndimension, which re-fingerprints every fastembed corpus, a migration, not a one-liner.",
        "source": "recall/fastembed-profile-id-is-hardcoded.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:40.898460+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5500669151504696,
        "confidence": 0.8479072817176957,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "9bef967347ccfe5e3082962b8e151ebe3d83fab5fef0799dbfafbc620428dcf8",
        "text": "So a live memory search embeds the query with voyage-4 and compares it against 8,716 bge-small\ndocument vectors. **Both models emit 1024 dimensions, so pgvector computes a cosine happily** and\nreturns a confidently ranked list that means nothing. No error, no warning, no failure code that\nnames it.\n\nRe-measure (the profile lives in the row's metadata, and mixing shows up as more than one value):\n\n```bash\npsql \"$RECALL_DSN\" -c \"SELECT tenant_id, metadata->>'embedding_profile' AS profile, count(*) \\\n  FROM chunks GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,3 DESC;\"\nssh vps2 \"ps -eo args | grep -o 'RECALL_TENANT=[^ ]* RECALL_EMBEDDER=[^ ]*' | sort -u\"\n```",
        "source": "recall/vps2-memory-tenant-mixes-three-embedders.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:02.180439+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5383456945419349,
        "confidence": 0.7734426356504502,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "345f3c331a1bbf8c16dea66bd35f6eaee82bfd829a8aa18be0f305946a4260d4",
        "text": "reported\r\n`corpus: 9552 chunks, 0 of them keyed by a Windows path`, so the adoption held across a day and\r\na further sync. The hazard is closed; this memo is now about the MECHANISM, which recurs\r\nwherever a corpus moves hosts, rather than about an open task.\r\n\r\n**The tenant's other defect was fixed in the same session, in the other direction from the one this\r\nmemo assumed.** It held two profiles at once (6,392 `bge-small-symmetric-v1`, 3,060 bge-large) while\r\nthe client queried it with `voyage-4`, so the corpus was re-embedded with **voyage-4** rather than\r\nthe client being pointed at bge-large: the sibling tenants already use it, and the alternative puts\r\na 1.4 GB ONNX model inside every stdio server session on that host. See\r\n[[vps2-memory-tenant-mixes-three-embedders]].",
        "source": "recall/vps2-memory-corpus-is-keyed-by-windows-paths.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:01.817439+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5139844111213449,
        "confidence": 0.5519500339913846,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "b654dc06d4310460a3417d778038aa27c00b9794b9fc066b63053586de9f16bb",
        "text": "1. **The label lies.** `recall_repos.chunks` for tenant `memory` reads\n   `embedding_profile=bge-small-symmetric-v1` while holding **1024-dim bge-large** vectors. Only\n   `vector_dims(embedding)` tells the truth.\n2. **The skip guard cannot see a model swap.** `index_fingerprint` =\n   `content_hash + embedding_profile_id + context_policy`. Two fastembed models of the SAME\n   dimension are indistinguishable to it, so re-indexing after a swap reports \"unchanged\" and\n   leaves the old vectors. Different dimensions are caught, but by pgvector's column type\n   erroring on insert, not by this guard.\n3. **A calibration bound to this profile cannot say which model it calibrated.** That is the\n   direct hazard for the bge-large pre-registration, whose whole point is bge-small \u2192 bge-large.",
        "source": "recall/fastembed-profile-id-is-hardcoded.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:40.915763+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5371437668800392,
        "confidence": 0.764509426007467,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "a7080b75bee43dccca727113a56d4fe532c92879d6c3048d62c40ab26fe4e1a0",
        "text": "1. **`RECALL_ENV=production` is required.** Without it the server uses the legacy store, which\n   knows nothing about generations, so every search reports `generation=None,\n   calibration_status=missing` and strict refuses. That symptom reads exactly like a broken\n   calibration and has been misdiagnosed as one before.\n2. **The embedder must be passed PER TENANT.** All three tenants are 1024-dimensional and all\n   three are different models. pgvector computes a cosine between any two 1024-vectors without\n   complaint, so the wrong embedder does not raise \u2014 it returns a confidently ranked list that\n   means nothing. A dimension match is not a model match.\n3. **The serving checkout must be at the database's migration level.** The DB is at 0016;\n   `~/recall-repos/engine` is recall 0.9.6 and",
        "source": "recall/recall-serves-trusted-from-vps2-over-ssh-stdio.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:52.272982+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,

        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **One embedding model per tenant.** Not a convention: it is the only thing standing between a\nmixed corpus and silently wrong retrieval. When a corpus wants a code model and a prose model,\nthat is two tenants, not one with two writers.\n\nFound on 2026-08-15 designing the `recall_repos` corpus on VPS2 (five repositories, code via\n`voyage-code-3`, docs via `voyage-4`). Ten tenants, `<repo>-code` and `<repo>-docs`, for exactly\nthis reason. The index driver asserts `code_embedder.dim == docs_embedder.dim` before writing,\nbecause both tenants share one table and one fixed vector width.\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f The same reasoning applies to the CHUNKER, but the failure is different and worse: see\n[[chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint]]. Related: [[guards-that-cannot-fail]],\n[[recall-corpus-name-boundary]].",
        "source": "recall/mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:45.166042+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,

        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"

      {
        "chunk_id": "ad407afb81ffbe3dd2ee8c1e07aded4d624969c80597ee525aca96a496c33bb3",
        "text": "`RetrievalDiagnostics.embedding_profile` (`recall/retriever.py:325`, `:471`) is **reported, never\nenforced**. Nothing in `recall/store.py` filters rows by it: the only occurrence is a `count(*)\nFILTER (WHERE NOT metadata ? 'embedding_profile')` used for a readiness report. So a tenant holding\npassages from two models is not an error state the code can see.\n\nIt is also not a *loud* failure, which is the part that matters. pgvector would reject a dimension\nmismatch, so two models of DIFFERENT width fail fast. The dangerous case is two models of the\n**same** width: `voyage-4` and `voyage-code-3` are both 1024, so a query embedded with one is\ncosine-compared against passages embedded with the other, the SQL succeeds, and the ranking is\ngarbage that looks exactly like a ranking.",
        "source": "recall/mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent.md",
        "ordinal": 0,

        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **Verify an embedder by `vector_dims(embedding)`, never by the profile label**: at least on\nthe fastembed path. Extends [[mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent]]: the field that was\nsupposed to make mixing detectable is itself inert, so that lesson is stronger than written.\n\nNot filed as a fix yet. The fix is to derive the default `profile_id` from model name plus\ndimension, which re-fingerprints every fastembed corpus, a migration, not a one-liner.",

        "text": "1. **The label lies.** `recall_repos.chunks` for tenant `memory` reads\n   `embedding_profile=bge-small-symmetric-v1` while holding **1024-dim bge-large** vectors. Only\n   `vector_dims(embedding)` tells the truth.\n2. **The skip guard cannot see a model swap.** `index_fingerprint` =\n   `content_hash + embedding_profile_id + context_policy`.         "text": "1. **`RECALL_ENV=production` is required.** Without it the server uses the legacy store, which\n   knows nothing about generations, so every search reports `generation=None,\n   calibration_status=missing` and strict refuses.         "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **One embedding model per tenant.** Not a convention: it is the only thing standing between a\nmixed corpus and silently wrong retrieval. When a corpus wants a code model and a prose model,\nthat is two tenants, not one with two writers.\n\nFound on 2026-08-15 designing the `recall_repos` corpus on VPS2 (five repositories, code via\n`voyage-code-3`, docs via `voyage-4`). Ten tenants, `<repo>-code` and `<repo>-docs`, for exactly\nthis reason. The index driver asserts `code_embedder.dim == docs_embedder.dim` before writing,\nbecause both tenants share one table and one fixed vector width.\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f The same reasoning applies to the CHUNKER, but the failure is different and worse: see\n[[chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint]]. Related: [[guards-that-cannot-fail]],\n[[recall-corpus-name-boundary]].",
        "source": "recall/mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:45.166042+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6652348837116442,
        "confidence": 0.9985533028779916,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "ad407afb81ffbe3dd2ee8c1e07aded4d624969c80597ee525aca96a496c33bb3",
        "text": "`RetrievalDiagnostics.embedding_profile` (`recall/retriever.py:325`, `:471`) is **reported, never\nenforced**. Nothing in `recall/store.py` filters rows by it: the only occurrence is a `count(*)\nFILTER (WHERE NOT metadata ? 'embedding_profile')` used for a readiness report. So a tenant holding\npassages from two models is not an error state the code can see.\n\nIt is also not a *loud* failure, which is the part that matters. pgvector would reject a dimension\nmismatch, so two models of DIFFERENT width fail fast. The dangerous case is two models of the\n**same** width: `voyage-4` and `voyage-code-3` are both 1024, so a query embedded with one is\ncosine-compared against passages embedded with the other, the SQL succeeds, and the ranking is\ngarbage that looks exactly like a ranking.",
        "source": "recall/mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:45.160230+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.613179523145549,
        "confidence": 0.9873700742945989,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "1bd4ead73b5ee728600f60c0ee6ba3fccfcd5296b5083ab003b1fc865cc9ac61",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **Verify an embedder by `vector_dims(embedding)`, never by the profile label**: at least on\nthe fastembed path. Extends [[mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent]]: the field that was\nsupposed to make mixing detectable is itself inert, so that lesson is stronger than written.\n\nNot filed as a fix yet. The fix is to derive the default `profile_id` from model name plus\ndimension, which re-fingerprints every fastembed corpus, a migration, not a one-liner.",
        "source": "recall/fastembed-profile-id-is-hardcoded.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:40.898460+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5500669151504696,
        "confidence": 0.8479072817176957,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "9bef967347ccfe5e3082962b8e151ebe3d83fab5fef0799dbfafbc620428dcf8",
        "text": "So a live memory search embeds the query with voyage-4 and compares it against 8,716 bge-small\ndocument vectors. **Both models emit 1024 dimensions, so pgvector computes a cosine happily** and\nreturns a confidently ranked list that means nothing. No error, no warning, no failure code that\nnames it.\n\nRe-measure (the profile lives in the row's metadata, and mixing shows up as more than one value):\n\n```bash\npsql \"$RECALL_DSN\" -c \"SELECT tenant_id, metadata->>'embedding_profile' AS profile, count(*) \\\n  FROM chunks GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,3 DESC;\"\nssh vps2 \"ps -eo args | grep -o 'RECALL_TENANT=[^ ]* RECALL_EMBEDDER=[^ ]*' | sort -u\"\n```",
        "source": "recall/vps2-memory-tenant-mixes-three-embedders.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:02.180439+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5383456945419349,
        "confidence": 0.7734426356504502,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "345f3c331a1bbf8c16dea66bd35f6eaee82bfd829a8aa18be0f305946a4260d4",
        "text": "reported\r\n`corpus: 9552 chunks, 0 of them keyed by a Windows path`, so the adoption held across a day and\r\na further sync. The hazard is closed; this memo is now about the MECHANISM, which recurs\r\nwherever a corpus moves hosts, rather than about an open task.\r\n\r\n**The tenant's other defect was fixed in the same session, in the other direction from the one this\r\nmemo assumed.** It held two profiles at once (6,392 `bge-small-symmetric-v1`, 3,060 bge-large) while\r\nthe client queried it with `voyage-4`, so the corpus was re-embedded with **voyage-4** rather than\r\nthe client being pointed at bge-large: the sibling tenants already use it, and the alternative puts\r\na 1.4 GB ONNX model inside every stdio server session on that host. See\r\n[[vps2-memory-tenant-mixes-three-embedders]].",
        "source": "recall/vps2-memory-corpus-is-keyed-by-windows-paths.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:01.817439+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5139844111213449,
        "confidence": 0.5519500339913846,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "b654dc06d4310460a3417d778038aa27c00b9794b9fc066b63053586de9f16bb",
        "text": "1. **The label lies.** `recall_repos.chunks` for tenant `memory` reads\n   `embedding_profile=bge-small-symmetric-v1` while holding **1024-dim bge-large** vectors. Only\n   `vector_dims(embedding)` tells the truth.\n2. **The skip guard cannot see a model swap.** `index_fingerprint` =\n   `content_hash + embedding_profile_id + context_policy`. Two fastembed models of the SAME\n   dimension are indistinguishable to it, so re-indexing after a swap reports \"unchanged\" and\n   leaves the old vectors. Different dimensions are caught, but by pgvector's column type\n   erroring on insert, not by this guard.\n3. **A calibration bound to this profile cannot say which model it calibrated.** That is the\n   direct hazard for the bge-large pre-registration, whose whole point is bge-small \u2192 bge-large.",
        "source": "recall/fastembed-profile-id-is-hardcoded.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:40.915763+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5371437668800392,
        "confidence": 0.764509426007467,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "a7080b75bee43dccca727113a56d4fe532c92879d6c3048d62c40ab26fe4e1a0",
        "text": "1. **`RECALL_ENV=production` is required.** Without it the server uses the legacy store, which\n   knows nothing about generations, so every search reports `generation=None,\n   calibration_status=missing` and strict refuses. That symptom reads exactly like a broken\n   calibration and has been misdiagnosed as one before.\n2. **The embedder must be passed PER TENANT.** All three tenants are 1024-dimensional and all\n   three are different models. pgvector computes a cosine between any two 1024-vectors without\n   complaint, so the wrong embedder does not raise \u2014 it returns a confidently ranked list that\n   means nothing. A dimension match is not a model match.\n3. **The serving checkout must be at the database's migration level.** The DB is at 0016;\n   `~/recall-repos/engine` is recall 0.9.6 and",
        "source": "recall/recall-serves-trusted-from-vps2-over-ssh-stdio.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:52.272982+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5135137712632836,
        "confidence": 0.5470753386301321,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "050bbbd7b0bb626e3aa15fb7939906571e05df8666e9f57a4768c1f706851e8c",
        "text": "Related: [[mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent]], [[no-pinned-revision-for-the-default-embedder]],\n[[calibrated-thresholds-and-the-overlap]].",
        "source": "recall/openrouter-embeddings-are-unlisted.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:46.515401+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.600473624453737,
        "confidence": 0.9786964603379879,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "0fe3b044518829ed448b45dd1a7181b70b3f1026b87495db08a17d738c5e6652",
        "text": "Measured 2026-08-20 on `recall_repos` (VPS2, port 55432) and from `ps` on that host.\n\n**Three different embedding models are in play on one tenant, and every layer is silent about it.**\n\n| where | model | rows |\n|---|---|---|\n| live MCP server's query embedder (`RECALL_EMBEDDER`) | `voyage:voyage-4` | n/a |\n| legacy `chunks`, which that server reads | `bge-small-symmetric-v1` | **8,716** |\n| same table, written 2026-08-19 | `voyage:voyage-4` | 2 |\n| `recall_chunks_v1` generation, which the calibration binds to | **bge-large** | 8,671 |",
        "source": "recall/vps2-memory-tenant-mixes-three-embedders.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:02.148520+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5611104630762073,
        "confidence": 0.8984713781900183,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "6306aaaccfe1f42773a7a08763fa202c0e69c6d8ed65e3aecdae976fdc28f818",
        "text": "\u26d4 **This is fatal, not merely suboptimal.** Own measurement, 2026-08-17: `voyage-4` scored\n0.269\u20130.413 on a corpus where `voyage-code-3` scored 0.480\u20130.834, recorded in\n[[calibrated-thresholds-and-the-overlap]] as \"'Voyage' is not an embedder; a threshold binds to the\nexact model.\" Cosines from different models are not on one scale, so neither ranking nor threshold\nsurvives the mix.\n\n**Cost of not knowing:** a calibration was measured and published on 2026-08-18 against the\nbge-large generation, and it was inert, because the serving path read a different table built with\na different model and queried it with a third. Diagnosing \"the corpus went stale\" would have fixed\nnothing.",
        "source": "recall/vps2-memory-tenant-mixes-three-embedders.md",

        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **One embedding model per tenant.** Not a convention: it is the only thing standing between a\nmixed corpus and silently wrong retrieval. When a corpus wants a code model and a prose model,\nthat is two tenants, not one with two writers.\n\nFound on 2026-08-15 designing the `recall_repos` corpus on VPS2 (five repositories, code via\n`voyage-code-3`, docs via `voyage-4`). Ten tenants, `<repo>-code` and `<repo>-docs`, for exactly\nthis reason. The index driver asserts `code_embedder.dim == docs_embedder.dim` before writing,\nbecause both tenants share one table and one fixed vector width.\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f The same reasoning applies to the CHUNKER, but the failure is different and worse: see\n[[chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint]]. Related: [[guards-that-cannot-fail]],\n[[recall-corpus-name-boundary]].",
        "source": "recall/mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent.md",

        "text": "`RetrievalDiagnostics.embedding_profile` (`recall/retriever.py:325`, `:471`) is **reported, never\nenforced**. Nothing in `recall/store.py` filters rows by it: the only occurrence is a `count(*)\nFILTER (WHERE NOT metadata ? 'embedding_profile')` used for a readiness report. So a tenant holding\npassages from two models is not an error state the code can see.\n\nIt is also not a *loud* failure, which is the part that matters. pgvector would reject a dimension\nmismatch, so two models of DIFFERENT width fail fast. The dangerous case is two models of the\n**same** width: `voyage-4` and `voyage-code-3` are both 1024, so a query embedded with one is\ncosine-compared against passages embedded with the other, the SQL succeeds, and the ranking is\ngarbage that looks exactly like a ranking.",

        "text": "1. **The label lies.** `recall_repos.chunks` for tenant `memory` reads\n   `embedding_profile=bge-small-symmetric-v1` while holding **1024-dim bge-large** vectors.         "text": "1. **`RECALL_ENV=production` is required.** Without it the server uses the legacy store, which\n   knows nothing about generations, so every search reports `generation=None,\n   calibration_status=missing` and strict refuses. That symptom reads exactly like a broken\n   calibration and has been misdiagnosed as one before.\n2. **The embedder must be passed PER TENANT.** All three tenants are 1024-dimensional and all\n   three are different models. pgvector computes a cosine between any two 1024-vectors without\n   complaint, so the wrong embedder does not raise \u2014 it returns a confidently ranked list that\n   means nothing. A dimension match is not a model match.\n3. **The serving checkout must be at the database's migration level.** The DB is at 0016;\n   `~/recall-repos/engine` is recall 0.9.6 and",

        "text": "Related: [[mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent]], [[no-pinned-revision-for-the-default-embedder]],\n[[calibrated-thresholds-and-the-overlap]].",

        "text": "Measured 2026-08-20 on `recall_repos` (VPS2, port 55432) and from `ps` on that host.\n\n**Three different embedding models are in play on one tenant, and every layer is silent about it.**\n\n| where | model | rows |\n|---|---|---|\n| live MCP server's query embedder (`RECALL_EMBEDDER`) | `voyage:voyage-4` | n/a |\n| legacy `chunks`, which that server reads | `bge-small-symmetric-v1` | **8,716** |\n| same table, written 2026-08-19 | `voyage:voyage-4` | 2 |\n| `recall_chunks_v1` generation, which the calibration binds to | **bge-large** | 8,671 |",

        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **One embedding model per tenant.** Not a convention: it is the only thing standing between a\nmixed corpus and silently wrong retrieval. When a corpus wants a code model and a prose model,\nthat is two tenants, not one with two writers.\n\nFound on 2026-08-15 designing the `recall_repos` corpus on VPS2 (five repositories, code via\n`voyage-code-3`, docs via `voyage-4`). Ten tenants, `<repo>-code` and `<repo>-docs`, for exactly\nthis reason. The index driver asserts `code_embedder.dim == docs_embedder.dim` before writing,\nbecause both tenants share one table and one fixed vector width.\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f The same reasoning applies to the CHUNKER, but the failure is different and worse: see\n[[chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint]]. Related: [[guards-that-cannot-fail]],\n[[recall-corpus-name-boundary]].",
        "source": "recall/mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:45.166042+00:00",

        "text": "`RetrievalDiagnostics.embedding_profile` (`recall/retriever.py:325`, `:471`) is **reported, never\nenforced**. Nothing in `recall/store.py` filters rows by it: the only occurrence is a `count(*)\nFILTER (WHERE NOT metadata ? 'embedding_profile')` used for a readiness report. So a tenant holding\npassages from two models is not an error state the code can see.\n\nIt is also not a *loud* failure, which is the part that matters. pgvector would reject a dimension\nmismatch, so two models of DIFFERENT width fail fast. The dangerous case is two models of the\n**same** width: `voyage-4` and `voyage-code-3` are both 1024, so a query embedded with one is\ncosine-compared against passages embedded with the other, the SQL succeeds, and the ranking is\ngarbage that looks exactly like a ranking.",
        "source": "recall/mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent.md",
        "ordinal": 0,

        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **Verify an embedder by `vector_dims(embedding)`, never by the profile label**: at least on\nthe fastembed path. Extends [[mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent]]: the field that was\nsupposed to make mixing detectable is itself inert, so that lesson is stronger than written.\n\nNot filed as a fix yet. The fix is to derive the default `profile_id` from model name plus\ndimension, which re-fingerprints every fastembed corpus, a migration, not a one-liner.",
        "source": "recall/fastembed-profile-id-is-hardcoded.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:40.898460+00:00",

      {
        "chunk_id": "9bef967347ccfe5e3082962b8e151ebe3d83fab5fef0799dbfafbc620428dcf8",
        "text": "So a live memory search embeds the query with voyage-4 and compares it against 8,716 bge-small\ndocument vectors. **Both models emit 1024 dimensions, so pgvector computes a cosine happily** and\nreturns a confidently ranked list that means nothing. No error, no warning, no failure code that\nnames it.\n\nRe-measure (the profile lives in the row's metadata, and mixing shows up as more than one value):\n\n```bash\npsql \"$RECALL_DSN\" -c \"SELECT tenant_id, metadata->>'embedding_profile' AS profile, count(*) \\\n  FROM chunks GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,3 DESC;\"\nssh vps2 \"ps -eo args | grep -o 'RECALL_TENANT=[^ ]* RECALL_EMBEDDER=[^ ]*' | sort -u\"\n```",

        "text": "reported\r\n`corpus: 9552 chunks, 0 of them keyed by a Windows path`, so the adoption held across a day and\r\na further sync. The hazard is closed; this memo is now about the MECHANISM, which recurs\r\nwherever a corpus moves hosts, rather than about an open task.\r\n\r\n**The tenant's other defect was fixed in the same session, in the other direction from the one this\r\nmemo assumed.** It held two profiles at once (6,392 `bge-small-symmetric-v1`, 3,060 bge-large) while\r\nthe client queried it with `voyage-4`, so the corpus was re-embedded with **voyage-4** rather than\r\nthe client being pointed at bge-large: the sibling tenants already use it, and the alternative puts\r\na 1.4 GB ONNX model inside every stdio server session on that host.         "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:01.817439+00:00",

      {
        "chunk_id": "b654dc06d4310460a3417d778038aa27c00b9794b9fc066b63053586de9f16bb",
        "text": "1. **The label lies.** `recall_repos.chunks` for tenant `memory` reads\n   `embedding_profile=bge-small-symmetric-v1` while holding **1024-dim bge-large** vectors. Only\n   `vector_dims(embedding)` tells the truth.\n2. **The skip guard cannot see a model swap.** `index_fingerprint` =\n   `content_hash + embedding_profile_id + context_policy`. Two fastembed models of the SAME\n   dimension are indistinguishable to it, so re-indexing after a swap reports \"unchanged\" and\n   leaves the old vectors. Different dimensions are caught, but by pgvector's column type\n   erroring on insert, not by this guard.\n3. **A calibration bound to this profile cannot say which model it calibrated.** That is the\n   direct hazard for the bge-large pre-registration, whose whole point is bge-small \u2192 bge-large.",
        "source": "recall/fastembed-profile-id-is-hardcoded.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
