        "text": "1. **`RECALL_ENV=production` is required.** Without it the server uses the legacy store, which\n   knows nothing about generations, so every search reports `generation=None,\n   calibration_status=missing` and strict refuses. That symptom reads exactly like a broken\n   calibration and has been misdiagnosed as one before.\n2. **The embedder must be passed PER TENANT.** All three tenants are 1024-dimensional and all\n   three are different models. pgvector computes a cosine between any two 1024-vectors without\n   complaint, so the wrong embedder does not raise \u2014 it returns a confidently ranked list that\n   means nothing. A dimension match is not a model match.\n3. **The serving checkout must be at the database's migration level.** The DB is at 0016;\n   `~/recall-repos/engine` is recall 0.9.6 and",
        "source": "recall/recall-serves-trusted-from-vps2-over-ssh-stdio.md",

        "text": "Related: [[mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent]], [[no-pinned-revision-for-the-default-embedder]],\n[[calibrated-thresholds-and-the-overlap]].",
        "source": "recall/openrouter-embeddings-are-unlisted.md",

      {

        "text": "Measured 2026-08-20 on `recall_repos` (VPS2, port 55432) and from `ps` on that host.\n\n**Three different embedding models are in play on one tenant, and every layer is silent about it.**\n\n| where | model | rows |\n|---|---|---|\n| live MCP server's query embedder (`RECALL_EMBEDDER`) | `voyage:voyage-4` | n/a |\n| legacy `chunks`, which that server reads | `bge-small-symmetric-v1` | **8,716** |\n| same table, written 2026-08-19 | `voyage:voyage-4` | 2 |\n| `recall_chunks_v1` generation, which the calibration binds to | **bge-large** | 8,671 |",
        "source": "recall/vps2-memory-tenant-mixes-three-embedders.md",

Diagnosing \"the corpus went stale\" would have fixed\nnothing.",

rows.payload:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "outcome": "abstained",
  "answer": null,
  "clarification_request": null,
  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "will re-indexing repair a chunker bug",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,
    "decision_state": "supported",
    "calibrated": true,
    "stale": false,
    "embedding_profile": "voyage:voyage-4",
    "retrieval_profile": "fast",
    "index_generation": "legacy",
    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "0c04d1b9834b1d8cddb3d52972cbba7127315a96bb0e911a07f4086f0d2c46e1",
        "text": "**The chunker is not in it.** So a file whose bytes have not changed is skipped even when the\nchunker that would now read it is a different one. Fixing a chunker-selection bug therefore does\n**not** repair an affected corpus by re-running `recall index`, the run reports \"N unchanged\" and\nleaves every wrongly-split chunk exactly where it was.\n\nTo actually rebuild, change one of the three terms (a different embedder, a different context\npolicy) or delete the affected sources first and let the next run re-read them.\n\nThe source docstring calls widening the tuple out as a migration rather than a comment change,\nbecause it re-fingerprints every indexed corpus at once. That is a real cost and the reason it has\nnot been done, not an oversight.",
        "source": "recall/chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:37.229499+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5980587362086031,
        "confidence": 0.9764846803780701,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "a3cd442d2c67a007fddda0eabb8cc6979d4c750af7dfca9ec86dfb399125de94",
        "text": "own corpus; shipped as designed in `recall setup`.\n- [Data as literals becomes corpus](data-as-literals-becomes-corpus.md) \u2014 the off-topic pool lived in a `.py` and so disqualified all 25 of its own subjects in any code corpus rooted here; a dogfood failure, not a user one.\n- [Chunker is not in the index fingerprint](chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint.md) \u2014 fixing a chunker bug does NOT repair the corpus; a re-index reports \"unchanged\" and leaves every wrong split in place.\n- [CI runs are silently not created](ci-runs-are-silently-not-created.md) \u2014 a dropped webhook means NO run; `gh pr checks` then serves the PREVIOUS run's job ids, so absent looks exactly like green.\n- [CI flake cluster: the ordering index served the unservable](ci-flake-cluster-planner-and-generations-tests.md) \u2014",
        "source": "recall/project_index.md",
        "ordinal": 7,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:48.355819+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5324216206325076,
        "confidence": 0.7271050667564398,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "47112135e2d9609b19470dcd40d54918f486c17419443b2ee34441310271f148",
        "text": "Found on 2026-08-15 fixing `recall index`, which chose the chunker from the GLOB SUFFIX\n(`chunk_code if args.glob.endswith(\".py\") else chunk_text`) rather than per file, so\n`--glob '**/*'` chunked every `.py` as prose and said nothing. Fixed by `chunker_for_path`, with\nthe non-repair noted in its docstring so the next person does not assume a re-index is enough.\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f `chunk_code` is **Python-specific**: it starts a block at a column-0 `def`/`class`/`@`/`async\ndef`. Given Rust, SQL or shell it matches nothing, returns one block, and is strictly worse than\n`chunk_text`, which at least splits on blank lines. Do not widen `PYTHON_SUFFIXES` without a\nchunker that parses the language being added.\n\n## Two consequences measured 2026-08-18",
        "source": "recall/chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:37.231143+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5392997586309776,
        "confidence": 0.7803611686593174,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "ec941cce98fd8f58e04a77f8e7a38826822f043d54167c6096c6c5452865b1de",
        "text": "Measured 2026-08-19, in recall's own memory corpus, using recall itself.\n\nA memo carried a \ud83d\udd01 correction at the top of the file retracting a claim in its middle. Searching\nfor that claim returned **the falsified paragraph on its own**, as chunk ordinal 7, with no trace of\nthe correction: retrieval returns **chunks**, and the correction was in a different one.\n\nThe second attempt failed too, and this is the part worth keeping. I inserted a \u26d4 retraction\nparagraph **immediately above** the falsified block, re-indexed, and re-ran the query. The chunker\ndoes not split on paragraph boundaries, so the retraction landed in the neighbouring chunk again and\nthe claim still came back naked.",
        "source": "recall/a-retraction-must-live-inside-the-chunk.md",
        "ordinal": 0,

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs only\n`ruff check .` plus bare `mypy`. `pyproject.toml` sets `[tool.ruff] line-length = 100` and nothing\nelse about formatting.\n\n**Why:** a `ruff format --check` failure on a file I am touching looks like a defect I introduced or\na nit worth clearing.         "text": "**How to apply:** run `python -m ruff check` to gate my work, never `ruff format`. If a format\nfailure appears on a file I edited, confirm it predates me (`git stash` then re-check) and leave it.\nReformatting is a repo-wide decision for the user, not a side effect of an unrelated change.\n\nRelated: [[ruff-blocked-locally]] for why it must be `python -m ruff` and not bare `ruff`.",

        "text": "and the merged follow-up banner fix in PR #368.\n- [ruff format is not this repo's convention](ruff-format-is-not-this-repos-convention.md) \u2014 348/406 files fail it; CI runs `ruff check` only, so never reformat.\n- [ruff runs here after all](ruff-blocked-locally.md) \u2014 CORRECTED: `python -m ruff` works (0.16.2, matches the repo pin); bare `ruff` is an old 0.6.9.\n- [session-db orphans reports a false clean](session-db-orphans-false-clean.md) \u2014 prints \"no orphaned containers\" when `docker` is not on PATH, and it fires exactly during session-close.\n- [Shared editable install across worktrees](shared-editable-install-across-worktrees.md) \u2014 one pip install serves ~18 worktrees; `python -m recall` from an unrelated dir silently runs the wrong checkout.\n- [Spawned task chips duplicate",

        "valid_from": null,

        "verdict": "ok",

      },

        "text": "*is* mypy), and then say \"blocked locally,\r\ngated in CI\" rather than \"mypy skipped\": a green CI job is a passing typecheck with an unusual\r\nevidence path, not a missing gate.\r\n\r\nRelated, still true: `ruff format --check` reports ~251 files would be reformatted in RE-call, and\r\nthat is **not a gate** \u2014 CI runs `ruff check` only. Separately the repo pins `ruff>=0.5,<0.16`\r\nbecause 0.16 stabilised new rules, so a local ruff 0.16 reports ~339 errors on unchanged code;\r\nconfirm a lint finding is yours by re-running with your changes stashed before reporting it.\r\n\r\n\ud83d\udd11 The general form, which is why this file now leads with a warning instead of a fact:\r\n**a memory asserting \"X cannot be done\" is the most expensive kind to leave unverified**, because\r\nit stops you retrying and so can never correct",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference-mypy-blocked-by-windows-app-control-2026-08-04.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:06:22.259152+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5544075304976108,
        "confidence": 0.8698798306745273,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "ebce158b9fd788681d4862244a1535b09ae33d91b334f7c9c0fbc7414cb5972b",
        "text": "Measured 2026-08-29 on PR #13: `ruff check .` printed \"All checks passed!\" here and CI went red in\n9 seconds, twice, on four findings the older binary does not know about (TRY004, RUF100 twice,\nI001).\n\nThe cause is two ruffs. `requirements-dev.txt` pins **ruff 0.16.2**, which is what CI installs and\nwhat `python -m ruff` resolves to in this checkout. The `ruff` on PATH is **0.6.9**, stale, and its\ndefault rule set is narrower. Both answer to the same command name, neither says which it is, and\nthe newer one is the one that decides whether the branch is mergeable.\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f The `ruff check .` line in this repository's own docs and in the CI workflow is therefore a\ntrap when read as a local instruction. Run it as a module:\n\n```bash\npython -m ruff check . && python -m ruff --version\n```",

        "text": "As of 2026-08-12 this repo has ~18 worktrees. The main checkout at\n`C:/Users/gde00/Documents/recall` usually sits on a feature branch (`codex/enterprise-rag-bench`\nwhen this was written), and **`master` is checked out in a separate worktree at\n`C:/Users/gde00/Documents/recall-suite-fix`**.\n\nSo `git checkout master` from the main checkout fails with *\"'master' is already used by worktree\nat ...\"*. To land work on master, operate on that worktree directly:\n\n```bash\ngit -C \"C:/Users/gde00/Documents/recall-suite-fix\" merge --squash <branch>\n```",
        "source": "recall/master-lives-in-a-separate-worktree.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:44.071158+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6026479242653903,
        "confidence": 0.9805129018555708,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "4ae396f7799e757ba2f55a2f1dfb6d3fe2f1f177d11731a5febdbe4373914d92",
        "text": "**Why this bit me:** I ran `git checkout master 2>&1 | tail -2 && git merge --squash <branch>`. The\npipe made `&&` read `tail`'s exit status, not the failed checkout's, so the squash merge ran against\nthe *feature branch* that happened to be checked out, leaving 13 staged additions and two\nconflicted files in the user's working tree. `git reset --hard HEAD` restored it because nothing was\ncommitted and the tree had been clean.\n\n**How to apply:** Check `git worktree list` before assuming any branch can be checked out. Never\npipe a command whose exit status gates a `&&` chain; capture the status explicitly instead. And\ncheck the target worktree is clean before merging into it.",
        "source": "recall/master-lives-in-a-separate-worktree.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:44.098338+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5163062810897827,
        "confidence": 0.5758358565318726,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "729ad74ba44fe2c474b19c1211aa99a42d305cc4b99b86900552a34312a701f0",
        "text": "local master, the branch ref stayed\n  at the old tip, and `git push` silently pushed **master's tip under the branch name** \u2014 surfacing\n  only as `gh pr create` \u2192 *\"No commits between master and \u2026\"*. An earlier edit to `checks.py` was\n  reverted the same way mid-session. **Check `git branch --show-current` immediately before commit\n  and push, and verify the remote ref with `git ls-remote` after.**\n  Cf. [[feedback-concurrent-sessions-race-the-same-clone-2026-07-24]].\n- \ud83d\udd11 **Fixing a doc can make it false.** LIMITS.md said \"checked 2026-07-31, master is NOT\n  protected\" \u2014 true when written, false ninety minutes later. PR #31 exists only to correct the\n  claim the previous PR introduced. A dated, confidently-stated fact needs an owner.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/project-mem-bench-adversarial-review-hardening-2026-07-31.md",
        "ordinal": 14,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:33.726199+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5408033406255648,
        "confidence": 0.7909537056483696,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "dcb0f7dc0ac15e6e3c6d003c435605a8b763d2a5fb95a37135a49b95cbe38e10",
        "text": "2. **`master` moved under a long-running session.** Two PRs (#1 quick-wins, #2 medium-effort)\n   implementing the *same* external audit landed from another session while work was in flight,\n   so a branch cut from `f72ac3e` conflicted. Check `git fetch` before assuming a branch base is\n   current on a repo with parallel sessions.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/project-recall-v040-cca-hardening-2026-07-21.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:40.066597+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5221847295761108,
        "confidence": 0.6345211771342857,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "70d5711bbaf7c50b061c7cc3f98d533516aaf24acaeffc7d22a0675c29e68118",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **Because master is parked in a worktree nobody routinely pulls, the LOCAL `master` ref is\nusually stale. Compare against `origin/master`, never `master`.** 2026-08-15 this nearly produced a\nbadly wrong report: `git log master..HEAD` said my branch was **24 commits** ahead and I was about\nto tell the user a PR would drag 18 unrelated commits along. Local `master` was 5 commits behind\n`origin/master`; against `origin/master` the real number was **10**. The tell was that the\n\"unrelated\" commits carried merged PR numbers (`(#333)`, `(#327)`) in their subjects, which a\ngenuinely unlanded commit does not have.",

query.query: does master allow merge commits

rows.payload:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "outcome": "abstained",
  "answer": null,
  "clarification_request": null,
  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "does master allow merge commits",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,
    "decision_state": "supported",
    "calibrated": true,
    "stale": false,
    "embedding_profile": "voyage:voyage-4",
    "retrieval_profile": "fast",
    "index_generation": "legacy",
    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "d2dd29bd476fe6b32e58e6f9c9705fdfc7bf83d377b5e7e0438b08d6f6fd61a5",
        "text": "**A third form, same root: a squash-merged branch looks unmerged forever.** Squashing rewrites the\ncontent into one new commit, so the source branch's original commits are never ancestors of master\nand `git log origin/master..HEAD` keeps listing them. \"5 commits ahead of master\" on such a branch\nis not evidence of pending work.\n\nMeasured 2026-08-18: I merged master into `claude/enterprise-rag-dense-floor`, reported it as \"worth\na second merge before it goes in\", and only checked afterwards that its PR #334 had been **merged\nthree days earlier**, squashed as `6ce37b4c`. The real additions over master were 10 insertions\nacross 14 files, not the 4 commits the log showed. Ask the forge, not the commit graph:",
        "source": "recall/bug-reports-from-stale-checkouts.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:36.538817+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5109475268062981,
        "confidence": 0.5203603544185555,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "fa27fb6500f7e4329d99a67d0724b3f3793d582681c7d6d89e74dbd3836b58dd",
        "text": "Caveat when squashing: GitHub pre-fills the message with the PR title plus a bullet per commit,\nwhich discards the commit body. This repo's history carries substantial commit bodies (see\n`git log`), so paste the real body in before confirming.\n\n**A SECOND rule, learned 2026-08-12 by pushing one:** the ruleset also forbids merge commits on\n`master`. Pushing a local `git merge --no-ff` printed\n\n```\nremote: Bypassed rule violations for refs/heads/master:\nremote: - This branch must not contain merge commits.\nremote:   Found 1 violation:  f8e8f21...\n```",
        "source": "recall/commit-signing-squash-merge.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.671946+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.587468301502962,
        "confidence": 0.9638476932852378,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "d71a3b7f85fdbb9a9eb947e7e1e4f64b7a6aef300050b1a81ad5c871c6e552b1",
        "text": "**How to apply:** ancestry against `HEAD` is never evidence about master. Ask the question that\nmatters, at the START and again before merging, and read it as a supersession signal:\n\ngit log --oneline HEAD..master -- <the files you are about to touch>\n\nAny output means someone changed those files ahead of you. `git merge-tree $(git merge-base HEAD\nmaster) HEAD master | grep \"changed in both\"` confirms it in one more command. And when a commit is\n\"not an ancestor\", the next command is `git branch -a --contains <sha>` INCLUDING master, not a\nconclusion.",
        "source": "recall/spawned-task-chips-duplicate-work.md",
        "ordinal": 6,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:54.314069+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5423978890417758,
        "confidence": 0.801771176774201,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "f3fe6fb1058b0d838a34fb7e96f7b2d443b9c3c4f71451660f4baf78ed340d4f",
        "text": "The push still landed on bypass, so this is a warning rather than a wall, but `master` now carries\na commit the repo's own ruleset rejects. That is worth knowing BEFORE choosing how to land work:\nsquash-merge satisfies both rules at once, which is probably why it was the recommended route in\nthe first place. The cost is real, though, and worth stating to the user rather than assuming:\nsquashing discards commit bodies AND collapses any `git merge` commits that deliberately preserve\nanother branch's history and authorship. When a branch is a consolidation of several branches,\nthat is the whole point of it, so ask which matters more instead of defaulting.",
        "source": "recall/commit-signing-squash-merge.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.683570+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5892699605661749,
        "confidence": 0.9663845402132778,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "b3c9a39e1bc586c52fc6a2b2c3913a88256bbf7470190dd5709d80c2357bedfc",
        "text": "1. **Before merging anything whose base is not `master`, expect the whole stack to go.** If that is\n   not wanted, retarget or cherry-pick first. The \"merge into the feature branch, then merge the\n   feature branch\" plan does not survive a stack.\n2. **Check the base is current.** Here `claude/audit-fixes-0-9-7` forked from `47640036` while\n   master had moved to `1c9bc1bc` (#433), a 21-file, 1,785-line gap. **Neither PR's CI ever tested\n   the combination that landed.** It happened to be green; that was luck, not evidence.\n   `git diff --stat origin/master <branch>` before merging says how big the untested delta is.\n3. **Verify master afterwards by per-job conclusions, not by the merge result.**",
        "source": "recall/stacked-prs-cascade-on-merge.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:54.452915+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5529032616076998,
        "confidence": 0.8625883665126854,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {

{

  "answer": null,
  "clarification_request": null,
  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "does master allow merge commits",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,
    "decision_state": "supported",

    "stale": false,

      {
        "chunk_id": "d2dd29bd476fe6b32e58e6f9c9705fdfc7bf83d377b5e7e0438b08d6f6fd61a5",
        "text": "**A third form, same root: a squash-merged branch looks unmerged forever.** Squashing rewrites the\ncontent into one new commit, so the source branch's original commits are never ancestors of master\nand `git log origin/master..HEAD` keeps listing them. \"5 commits ahead of master\" on such a branch\nis not evidence of pending work.\n\nMeasured 2026-08-18: I merged master into `claude/enterprise-rag-dense-floor`, reported it as \"worth\na second merge before it goes in\", and only checked afterwards that its PR #334 had been **merged\nthree days earlier**, squashed as `6ce37b4c`. The real additions over master were 10 insertions\nacross 14 files, not the 4 commits the log showed. Ask the forge, not the commit graph:",
        "source": "recall/bug-reports-from-stale-checkouts.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:36.538817+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5109475268062981,
        "confidence": 0.5203603544185555,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "fa27fb6500f7e4329d99a67d0724b3f3793d582681c7d6d89e74dbd3836b58dd",
        "text": "Caveat when squashing: GitHub pre-fills the message with the PR title plus a bullet per commit,\nwhich discards the commit body. This repo's history carries substantial commit bodies (see\n`git log`), so paste the real body in before confirming.\n\n**A SECOND rule, learned 2026-08-12 by pushing one:** the ruleset also forbids merge commits on\n`master`. Pushing a local `git merge --no-ff` printed\n\n```\nremote: Bypassed rule violations for refs/heads/master:\nremote: - This branch must not contain merge commits.\nremote:   Found 1 violation:  f8e8f21...\n```",
        "source": "recall/commit-signing-squash-merge.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.671946+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.587468301502962,
        "confidence": 0.9638476932852378,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "d71a3b7f85fdbb9a9eb947e7e1e4f64b7a6aef300050b1a81ad5c871c6e552b1",
        "text": "**How to apply:** ancestry against `HEAD` is never evidence about master. Ask the question that\nmatters, at the START and again before merging, and read it as a supersession signal:\n\ngit log --oneline HEAD..master -- <the files you are about to touch>\n\nAny output means someone changed those files ahead of you. `git merge-tree $(git merge-base HEAD\nmaster) HEAD master | grep \"changed in both\"` confirms it in one more command. And when a commit is\n\"not an ancestor\", the next command is `git branch -a --contains <sha>` INCLUDING master, not a\nconclusion.",
        "source": "recall/spawned-task-chips-duplicate-work.md",
        "ordinal": 6,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:54.314069+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5423978890417758,
        "confidence": 0.801771176774201,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "f3fe6fb1058b0d838a34fb7e96f7b2d443b9c3c4f71451660f4baf78ed340d4f",
        "text": "The push still landed on bypass, so this is a warning rather than a wall, but `master` now carries\na commit the repo's own ruleset rejects. That is worth knowing BEFORE choosing how to land work:\nsquash-merge satisfies both rules at once, which is probably why it was the recommended route in\nthe first place. The cost is real, though, and worth stating to the user rather than assuming:\nsquashing discards commit bodies AND collapses any `git merge` commits that deliberately preserve\nanother branch's history and authorship. When a branch is a consolidation of several branches,\nthat is the whole point of it, so ask which matters more instead of defaulting.",
        "source": "recall/commit-signing-squash-merge.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:38.683570+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5892699605661749,
        "confidence": 0.9663845402132778,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "b3c9a39e1bc586c52fc6a2b2c3913a88256bbf7470190dd5709d80c2357bedfc",
        "text": "1. **Before merging anything whose base is not `master`, expect the whole stack to go.** If that is\n   not wanted, retarget or cherry-pick first. The \"merge into the feature branch, then merge the\n   feature branch\" plan does not survive a stack.\n2. **Check the base is current.** Here `claude/audit-fixes-0-9-7` forked from `47640036` while\n   master had moved to `1c9bc1bc` (#433), a 21-file, 1,785-line gap. **Neither PR's CI ever tested\n   the combination that landed.** It happened to be green; that was luck, not evidence.\n   `git diff --stat origin/master <branch>` before merging says how big the untested delta is.\n3. **Verify master afterwards by per-job conclusions, not by the merge result.**",
        "source": "recall/stacked-prs-cascade-on-merge.md",
        "ordinal": 3,

        "text": "`origin/master` moved **28 commits in one session**, twice, the second time in the minutes between\nthe first merge and opening the PR. **Merge, do not rebase**: four commits would each have had to\nresolve the same shared-document conflicts.\n\n\ud83d\udd11 Resolve by **reconstruction with assertions**, never by editing markers: read upstream's copy,\ninsert your entry, then assert upstream survives byte for byte (length + content), rather than\nreading the diff. See [[feedback-concurrent-sessions-race-the-same-clone-2026-07-24]].\n\n## \ud83e\uddea Two mutation-harness rules that cost time to learn",

        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f Note the asymmetry that makes this dangerous: a cannot-fail guard produces a **false green**,\nand a cannot-pass guard produces a **false red** that discards good work. I produced one of each in\nthe same session.\n\nRelated: [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] (the twin) \u00b7\n[[feedback-a-guard-must-hold-on-its-own-output-2026-08-05]] \u00b7\n[[project-recall-mtrag-retrieval-coverage-bottleneck-2026-08-06]] (where all three occurred)",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-check-the-deciding-cell-has-power-2026-08-06.md",
        "ordinal": 5,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:15.809843+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6426203676914776,
        "confidence": 0.996281873696258,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "bac25f19474642109d42944aa9c0c4799192203d267492e8330b9ba8914a85bc",
        "text": "Un guard non \u00e8 finito quando i suoi controlli passano. \u00c8 finito quando la cosa che **restituisce**\nsoddisfa ancora quei controlli.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-hold-on-its-own-output-2026-08-05.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:13.987838+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6273651719093323,
        "confidence": 0.992983974620368,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "84d3077c1fe9b7bf4a99eef0eec9e662fa6eadabc1be42b4982cadb1f0360bce",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 The sharper version of the standing lesson: *a guard that reads as protection and cannot fire*\nhas a twin \u2014 **a guard that cannot PASS**. Both look like rigour in a document and neither tests\nanything. Asking \"what would make this fire?\" catches the first; **\"what would make this pass?\"**\nis the question I was not asking.\n\n## What it cost, and what caught it\n\n`bug-auditor` caught F3 (before publication) and would have caught C4; D1 I caught only because I\nran the check anyway. The direct cost was a verdict claiming a \"textbook\" control that was 96%\narithmetic, and a FALSIFIED verdict on a perfectly valid run. **Two of three were caught before\nanything shipped \u2014 by the audit, not by me.**",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-check-the-deciding-cell-has-power-2026-08-06.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:15.827969+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6178515412984485,
        "confidence": 0.989589319674786,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "eec41629f616f5a2ff7265198388f4308798a1baca5e0f6cc67b3a0011974d1d",
        "text": "**Why:** [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] covers guards that never fire because the assertion was\nunsatisfiable or too narrow from the start. This is the adjacent failure: a guard that used to\nfire, and quietly stops, because it depends on a string/event contract nobody versioned. The\nguard-test in that memory (mutate and watch it go red) catches the first kind but not this one,\nbecause the mutation target is the code under test, not the upstream tool the gate depends on.",
        "source": "recall/verifier-canary-liveness.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:56.737372+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5980635463614331,
        "confidence": 0.9764893013746497,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "2527d537b7feb48b38cd3b69bf0811d7ed45eddc79376caae313433656152d0b",
        "text": "**Why:** the credibility of a guard is a shared resource. Every false alarm spends it, and it is\nspent silently, so the guard still looks installed long after it stopped being believed.\n\n**How to apply:** when a guard contradicts something you have directly observed, treat that as a\nbug report against the guard and open its source before dismissing it. Check specifically whether\nthe parse failure disables a detection further down, since an early return on unparsed input is the\nusual shape. And when a guard's regex is the guard, keep its cases in the file and make them\nrunnable. Related: [[guards-that-cannot-fail]],\n[[bug-reports-from-stale-checkouts]], [[missing-input-becomes-a-clean-null]].",
        "source": "recall/a-guard-that-cries-wolf-is-worse-than-none.md",

        "text": "funder wallet): `post_exit_7d` is a lower bound, so a low ratio is confounded \u21d2 NEEDS_DATA not a false FAIL. To resolve: build a **post-exit pool reward-RATE source** (gamma per-market rate after exit), else close as NEEDS_DATA.\n- \ud83d\udd11 #1896 and #1897 are deliberately opposed \u2014 cannot both PASS. A PASS re-arms nothing (lane closed #1804, maker halted `_RMK_KILL`).\n\n## 5. \u00a72b deadman checks (local scheduled tasks)\n`gate-check-1895-2026-07-30`, `gate-check-1897-2026-07-30`, `gate-check-1896-2026-08-06` \u2014 each runs the gate-check + posts the verdict (run when the app is open / next launch).",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/project-lrp-gate-work-2026-07-19.md",
        "ordinal": 5,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:32.936348+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5550750659428559,
        "confidence": 0.8730087094952274,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "b1e319607401c01d2645d5614aa5f0cbf541a9dab0967c4b83f5c0d1c62094b2",
        "text": "**Why:** CLAUDE.md \u00a72b makes every gate carry a scheduled check as its deadman, but there is no\ninverse rule. An orphaned deadman is worse than a missing one: it arrives with confident,\nself-contained instructions and no knowledge that the lane died, so the default behaviour is to\nre-run a closed experiment and post numbers that invite a reopen. The scheduled task's own\nframing is stale data, not authority \u2014 [[feedback-verify-collector-terminal-table-2026-07-14]]\nis the same failure shape one layer down.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-closing-a-gate-early-must-cancel-its-scheduled-check-2026-07-21.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:15.866789+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6133376542728443,
        "confidence": 0.9874523175821098,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "87360cf238b9be73104d1ced608462149da32db54da70e47051274df296ecf84",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n1. On arming any probe, note the **terminal table** the gate query reads (e.g. `polymarket_live_orders`, `*_fills`) \u2014 not the signals or dry-ledger table.\n2. Within 24-48h, run `SELECT count(*), max(<ts>) FROM <terminal_table> WHERE <edge_id/slug filter> AND <ts> >= <arm_date>`. Zero rows \u21d2 **not armed** \u2014 fix or close, do not let it ride to the gate date.\n3. Sanity-check the whole `systemd-analyze cat-config` view of the unit, not just the base unit file \u2014 drop-ins (`*.d/*.conf`) override `Environment=`, and a later `EnvironmentFile=` can too ([[reference_systemd_environmentfile_overrides_environment_2026-07-12]]).\n4. Every gate issue must have a paired scheduled check (CLAUDE.md Session-Close \u00a72b). #1594 had none, which is why it drifted 13 days unnoticed.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-verify-collector-terminal-table-2026-07-14.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:18.778721+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5302005288184164,
        "confidence": 0.7082813135554336,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "baa846d2844718d3a3590b39f318bec6071bfd8e1c5c3649e484e5d4abbb0d30",
        "text": "Closing a `gate` issue early (lane death, venue repricing, moot verdict) leaves its paired\n`/schedule` deadman armed. On 2026-07-21 the `maker-net-tuner-gate-run` task fired for gate\n#1494 \u2014 closed 2026-07-16 with the LRP lane. The task instructions still read as a live gate\n(\"ahead of the 2026-07-21 gate\") and prescribed training + posting a learned-vs-baseline\nverdict.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-closing-a-gate-early-must-cancel-its-scheduled-check-2026-07-21.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:15.857847+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6259298288163393,
        "confidence": 0.9925529431724239,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "e3c2c95967af3f2506d9a8d5867adf3d12d68c8a70c1f2d3197cf3308da501b5",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n- Session-Close \u00a72c (gate resolved \u2192 comment + close) is incomplete: also **cancel or repoint\n  the paired scheduled check** in the same session.\n- When a scheduled gate task fires, **read the issue state FIRST**. `state: CLOSED` \u21d2 the correct\n  output is a SUPERSEDED note on the issue, not a run.\n- Do not treat \"the run is technically feasible\" as a reason to run. #1494's substrate was still\n  writing and the tuner still imported cleanly; the blocker was economic (`rewardsMinSize`\n  20\u2192200 priced us out), and no allocator result could move it.\n  See [[project-lrp-reward-farming-closed-venue-repricing-2026-07-16]] and\n  [[feedback-venue-can-reprice-you-out-overnight-2026-07-16]].",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-closing-a-gate-early-must-cancel-its-scheduled-check-2026-07-21.md",

Fix = utente (ri-autorizza claude.ai/code). \ud83d\udd11 **una data di gate non prova che un check partir\u00e0.** \u2705 Rimpiazzo: timer VPS3 \u2192 verdetto in TABELLA. [[incident-cloud-routines-all-auto-disabled-repo-access-2026-07-30]]\r\n- \u2705 **#1895 RIAPERTA + deadman shippato \u2014 nessuna decisione fino al 08-13** (`gate-1895-check.timer` VPS3 \u2192 `gate_1895_check_log`). \u26a0\ufe0f i fill pre-15:47Z sono sotto il drain print-only. [[project-gate-1895-touch-needs-data-markout-never-written-2026-07-30]]\r\n- \ud83d\udd34\ud83d\udd34 **#1761 NEEDS_DATA \u2192 09-04, ma la lane BTC 15m NON accumula pi\u00f9**: `updown-lag-racer` \u00e8 `active` e ticchetta con **`enter=0`, `outside_window` 100%** dal 07-31 \u21d2 **zero fill dal 07-23**; estendere non serve finch\u00e9 il fill path \u00e8 rotto. \ud83d\udd34 **APERTA: chi ha messo `notional_usd=15`**",

        "text": "**Refusing known-BAD values is a negative check. It closes only the failure modes you thought of,\nand everything the producer never emits \u2014 or that predates the field \u2014 walks straight through.**\n\nMeasured, RE-call `fix/beam-artifact-rejudgeable`, 2026-08-07. I wrote `embed_parity.py` to stop a\nGPU-vs-CPU comparison silently running CPU-vs-CPU. Three guards in it could not fire:",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-require-good-not-refuse-bad-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:14.059120+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6086865793092942,
        "confidence": 0.9847976562062956,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "f4bf4e69226c1d8f0d47ec7979d99985a4c2181e97abba6416456adcf37f4ef5",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 The closed form is `if meta.get(\"providers_source\") != \"session\": refuse` \u2014 require the\nknown-good value. It rejects nothing the producer emits and everything it does not.\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **A test that hand-crafts an input the producer cannot produce is not a test of the guard.**\nThat is how #3 shipped green.\n\n\u2194 Same family as [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] and\n[[feedback-check-the-deciding-cell-has-power-2026-08-06]]. What is new here is the *repair*\ninheriting the defect, and that only an audit by other agents caught it.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-require-good-not-refuse-bad-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:14.081384+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5863803132033721,
        "confidence": 0.9622275154086811,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "c7710c6887a9c186773a9eccd7880f412af38ce561ab97667e776db2de9699d9",
        "text": "- **A pre-filter may be sloppy; a decision may not.** The `case` in `settings.json` that decides\n  whether to *invoke* a guard can over-match harmlessly, because the script then decides. The script\n  itself cannot.\n- **One residual false positive is known and left in place.** Backticks inside single quotes are not\n  command substitution to a shell, but the parser treats them as such. It over-detects, which is the\n  safe direction for a guard, and it is documented rather than silently accepted.\n\nRelated: [[test-a-guards-allow-path]] is the same session's other half, a guard refusing correct\nwork. [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] is the opposite failure. [[a-detector-with-no-sink]] completes the\nset: fires and is discarded, fires wrongly, never fires.",
        "source": "recall/parse-commands-do-not-match-text.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:46.823291+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5561231706215851,
        "confidence": 0.8777915308580624,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "2f6cb48db80920615da9c06f55508b653f4a0caa7815ea4a2c884079d970dd36",
        "text": "- **Enumerate mutants from the SOURCE, top to bottom, not from the guards you remember.** I once\n  mutated 25 guards, reached 24/25 and called it verified; an auditor enumerated from the file,\n  ran 51, and 26 survived, including the identity cross-check the whole design existed for\n  (it compared one of its four columns) and a type loop whose deletion makes a bad row *served as\n  a hit* rather than refused.\n- **A guard with a long comment defending it is a positive signal it is untested.** The author\n  explained it instead of pinning it. `rollback()`, a `close()` on the refusal path, and an mkdir\n  block were each argued for at length and pinned by nothing.\n- **A guard with N conjoined terms needs N tests, one per term.** A single test can only ever see\n  one term, because it varies one",
        "source": "recall/guards-that-cannot-fail.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:42.710215+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5298556405219826,
        "confidence": 0.7052907687701772,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "7cccba84a63aff61faa5ebab8e33ae791b7c3f59f4b471028cf857fc54a7d386",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f Note the asymmetry that makes this dangerous: a cannot-fail guard produces a **false green**,\nand a cannot-pass guard produces a **false red** that discards good work. I produced one of each in\nthe same session.\n\nRelated: [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] (the twin) \u00b7\n[[feedback-a-guard-must-hold-on-its-own-output-2026-08-05]] \u00b7\n[[project-recall-mtrag-retrieval-coverage-bottleneck-2026-08-06]] (where all three occurred)",

        "text": "**Refusing known-BAD values is a negative check. It closes only the failure modes you thought of,\nand everything the producer never emits \u2014 or that predates the field \u2014 walks straight through.**\n\nMeasured, RE-call `fix/beam-artifact-rejudgeable`, 2026-08-07. I wrote `embed_parity.py` to stop a\nGPU-vs-CPU comparison silently running CPU-vs-CPU. Three guards in it could not fire:",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-require-good-not-refuse-bad-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:14.059120+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6086865793092942,
        "confidence": 0.9847976562062956,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "f4bf4e69226c1d8f0d47ec7979d99985a4c2181e97abba6416456adcf37f4ef5",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 The closed form is `if meta.get(\"providers_source\") != \"session\": refuse` \u2014 require the\nknown-good value. It rejects nothing the producer emits and everything it does not.\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **A test that hand-crafts an input the producer cannot produce is not a test of the guard.**\nThat is how #3 shipped green.\n\n\u2194 Same family as [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] and\n[[feedback-check-the-deciding-cell-has-power-2026-08-06]]. What is new here is the *repair*\ninheriting the defect, and that only an audit by other agents caught it.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-require-good-not-refuse-bad-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:14.081384+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5863803132033721,
        "confidence": 0.9622275154086811,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "c7710c6887a9c186773a9eccd7880f412af38ce561ab97667e776db2de9699d9",
        "text": "- **A pre-filter may be sloppy; a decision may not.** The `case` in `settings.json` that decides\n  whether to *invoke* a guard can over-match harmlessly, because the script then decides. The script\n  itself cannot.\n- **One residual false positive is known and left in place.** Backticks inside single quotes are not\n  command substitution to a shell, but the parser treats them as such. It over-detects, which is the\n  safe direction for a guard, and it is documented rather than silently accepted.\n\nRelated: [[test-a-guards-allow-path]] is the same session's other half, a guard refusing correct\nwork. [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] is the opposite failure. [[a-detector-with-no-sink]] completes the\nset: fires and is discarded, fires wrongly, never fires.",
        "source": "recall/parse-commands-do-not-match-text.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:46.823291+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5561231706215851,
        "confidence": 0.8777915308580624,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "2f6cb48db80920615da9c06f55508b653f4a0caa7815ea4a2c884079d970dd36",
        "text": "- **Enumerate mutants from the SOURCE, top to bottom, not from the guards you remember.** I once\n  mutated 25 guards, reached 24/25 and called it verified; an auditor enumerated from the file,\n  ran 51, and 26 survived, including the identity cross-check the whole design existed for\n  (it compared one of its four columns) and a type loop whose deletion makes a bad row *served as\n  a hit* rather than refused.\n- **A guard with a long comment defending it is a positive signal it is untested.** The author\n  explained it instead of pinning it. `rollback()`, a `close()` on the refusal path, and an mkdir\n  block were each argued for at length and pinned by nothing.\n- **A guard with N conjoined terms needs N tests, one per term.** A single test can only ever see\n  one term, because it varies one",
        "source": "recall/guards-that-cannot-fail.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:42.710215+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5298556405219826,
        "confidence": 0.7052907687701772,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },

        "chunk_id": "7cccba84a63aff61faa5ebab8e33ae791b7c3f59f4b471028cf857fc54a7d386",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f Note the asymmetry that makes this dangerous: a cannot-fail guard produces a **false green**,\nand a cannot-pass guard produces a **false red** that discards good work. I produced one of each in\nthe same session.\n\nRelated: [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] (the twin) \u00b7\n[[feedback-a-guard-must-hold-on-its-own-output-2026-08-05]] \u00b7\n[[project-recall-mtrag-retrieval-coverage-bottleneck-2026-08-06]] (where all three occurred)",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-check-the-deciding-cell-has-power-2026-08-06.md",
        "ordinal": 5,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:15.809843+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5979035736379973,
        "confidence": 0.9763351431279611,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "eec41629f616f5a2ff7265198388f4308798a1baca5e0f6cc67b3a0011974d1d",
        "text": "**Why:** [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] covers guards that never fire because the assertion was\nunsatisfiable or too narrow from the start. This is the adjacent failure: a guard that used to\nfire, and quietly stops, because it depends on a string/event contract nobody versioned.         "source": "recall/verifier-canary-liveness.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:56.737372+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5897769859233787,
        "confidence": 0.9670669242347618,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "bac25f19474642109d42944aa9c0c4799192203d267492e8330b9ba8914a85bc",
        "text": "Un guard non \u00e8 finito quando i suoi controlli passano. \u00c8 finito quando la cosa che **restituisce**\nsoddisfa ancora quei controlli.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-hold-on-its-own-output-2026-08-05.md",

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "outcome": "abstained",
  "answer": null,
  "clarification_request": null,
  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "is it enough for a guard to refuse known-bad values",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,
    "decision_state": "supported",

      {
        "chunk_id": "7627a6144867fa9a52b6d8fe0e77256ee89910be74868c79b4592c375ce411ad",
        "text": "**Refusing known-BAD values is a negative check. It closes only the failure modes you thought of,\nand everything the producer never emits \u2014 or that predates the field \u2014 walks straight through.**\n\nMeasured, RE-call `fix/beam-artifact-rejudgeable`, 2026-08-07. I wrote `embed_parity.py` to stop a\nGPU-vs-CPU comparison silently running CPU-vs-CPU. Three guards in it could not fire:",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-require-good-not-refuse-bad-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:14.059120+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6086865793092942,
        "confidence": 0.9847976562062956,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "f4bf4e69226c1d8f0d47ec7979d99985a4c2181e97abba6416456adcf37f4ef5",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 The closed form is `if meta.get(\"providers_source\") != \"session\": refuse` \u2014 require the\nknown-good value. It rejects nothing the producer emits and everything it does not.\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **A test that hand-crafts an input the producer cannot produce is not a test of the guard.**\nThat is how #3 shipped green.\n\n\u2194 Same family as [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] and\n[[feedback-check-the-deciding-cell-has-power-2026-08-06]]. What is new here is the *repair*\ninheriting the defect, and that only an audit by other agents caught it.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-a-guard-must-require-good-not-refuse-bad-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:14.081384+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5863803132033721,
        "confidence": 0.9622275154086811,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "c7710c6887a9c186773a9eccd7880f412af38ce561ab97667e776db2de9699d9",
        "text": "- **A pre-filter may be sloppy; a decision may not.** The `case` in `settings.json` that decides\n  whether to *invoke* a guard can over-match harmlessly, because the script then decides. The script\n  itself cannot.\n- **One residual false positive is known and left in place.** Backticks inside single quotes are not\n  command substitution to a shell, but the parser treats them as such. It over-detects, which is the\n  safe direction for a guard, and it is documented rather than silently accepted.\n\nRelated: [[test-a-guards-allow-path]] is the same session's other half, a guard refusing correct\nwork. [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] is the opposite failure. [[a-detector-with-no-sink]] completes the\nset: fires and is discarded, fires wrongly, never fires.",
        "source": "recall/parse-commands-do-not-match-text.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:46.823291+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5561231706215851,
        "confidence": 0.8777915308580624,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "2f6cb48db80920615da9c06f55508b653f4a0caa7815ea4a2c884079d970dd36",
        "text": "- **Enumerate mutants from the SOURCE, top to bottom, not from the guards you remember.** I once\n  mutated 25 guards, reached 24/25 and called it verified; an auditor enumerated from the file,\n  ran 51, and 26 survived, including the identity cross-check the whole design existed for\n  (it compared one of its four columns) and a type loop whose deletion makes a bad row *served as\n  a hit* rather than refused.\n- **A guard with a long comment defending it is a positive signal it is untested.** The author\n  explained it instead of pinning it. `rollback()`, a `close()` on the refusal path, and an mkdir\n  block were each argued for at length and pinned by nothing.\n- **A guard with N conjoined terms needs N tests, one per term.** A single test can only ever see\n  one term, because it varies one",
        "source": "recall/guards-that-cannot-fail.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:04:42.710215+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5298556405219826,
        "confidence": 0.7052907687701772,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "7cccba84a63aff61faa5ebab8e33ae791b7c3f59f4b471028cf857fc54a7d386",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f Note the asymmetry that makes this dangerous: a cannot-fail guard produces a **false green**,\nand a cannot-pass guard produces a **false red** that discards good work. I produced one of each in\nthe same session.\n\nRelated: [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] (the twin) \u00b7\n[[feedback-a-guard-must-hold-on-its-own-output-2026-08-05]] \u00b7\n[[project-recall-mtrag-retrieval-coverage-bottleneck-2026-08-06]] (where all three occurred)",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-check-the-deciding-cell-has-power-2026-08-06.md",

        "valid_from": null,

        "cosine": 0.5979035736379973,
        "confidence": 0.9763351431279611,

      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "eec41629f616f5a2ff7265198388f4308798a1baca5e0f6cc67b3a0011974d1d",
        "text": "**Why:** [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] covers guards that never fire because the assertion was\nunsatisfiable or too narrow from the start. This is the adjacent failure: a guard that used to\nfire, and quietly stops, because it depends on a string/event contract nobody versioned. The\nguard-test in that memory (mutate and watch it go red) catches the first kind but not this one,\nbecause the mutation target is the code under test, not the upstream tool the gate depends on.",

query.query: does a clean git status mean I am on the tip of the branch

rows.payload:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "outcome": "abstained",
  "answer": null,
  "clarification_request": null,
  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "does a clean git status mean I am on the tip of the branch",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,
    "decision_state": "supported",
    "calibrated": true,
    "stale": false,
    "embedding_profile": "voyage:voyage-4",
    "retrieval_profile": "fast",
    "index_generation": "legacy",
    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "71f9364ff8e50113cf589a02d531372e38e6b66f87e39e38b3e2f31e24212990",
        "text": "## Why the usual checks did not catch it\n- `git status --short` was **clean** \u2014 and clean says nothing about *which commit* you are on.\n- The empirical test was real, reproducible, and executed the actual function. Running the code is\n  normally the strongest evidence available; here it faithfully measured **the wrong tree**.\n- Three sibling clones exist (`~/Documents/RE-call`, `re-call`, `recall`) on different branches.\n  Picking one by name and finding a git repo is not picking the right one.\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **Evidence quality does not survive a wrong substrate.** Verifying harder (running vs reading)\nmade the false finding *more* convincing, not less.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-check-head-vs-origin-before-reading-code-2026-07-24.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:15.665163+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5135411620140076,
        "confidence": 0.5473592976465647,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "89c957e7780510bec9cccec5df5997ae17de68d1450121e414fed3f76c5ca915",
        "text": "twice. It was\r\n   already **MERGED** (`8cf35c5`) and the branch deleted.\r\n\r\nNothing was lost and master went green \u2014 but every one of those steps *looked like a failure* from\r\ninside my session.\r\n\r\n**Why:** the dangerous reading is the inverse of the truth. `nothing to commit, working tree clean`\r\nnormally means \"my edit didn't apply\"; here it meant \"my edit applied and someone else committed\r\nit\". `mergeable: UNKNOWN` normally means \"GitHub is still computing\"; here it meant \"the PR is\r\nclosed\". Reacting to either at face value leads to re-doing landed work, or worse, force-pushing\r\nover it. This is the same family as [[feedback-check-head-vs-origin-before-reading-code-2026-07-24]]\r\n\u2014 a wrong picture of the tree \u2014 but the opposite direction: there the checkout was *behind* origin,\r\nhere",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback-concurrent-sessions-race-the-same-clone-2026-07-24.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:16.091770+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5497561156459032,
        "confidence": 0.8462226601064032,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "830eac37fe7804ce977c065bb68245c24c0fa3605aa7c83c2eeeba0d0d8c3d27",
        "text": "is a SNAPSHOT, and it rots inside the session\r\n\r\nThe hook that claims the workspace prints a line like `vs origin/master  0 behind, 0 ahead`. Reacting to either at face value leads to re-doing landed work, or worse, force-pushing\r\nover it. This is the same family as [[feedback-check-head-vs-origin-before-reading-code-2026-07-24]]\r\n\u2014 a wrong picture of the tree \u2014 but the opposite direction: there the checkout was *behind* origin,\r\nhere",

        "ordinal": 1,

        "valid_from": null,

        "text": "Before deploying any sudoers lockdown that replaces wildcard `NOPASSWD: ALL` with a Cmnd_Alias allowlist, **verify whether the target user has a password set**. Without one, sudo for any non-allowlisted command silently fails with \"a terminal is required to read the password\" \u2014 the operator is locked out of every ad-hoc admin operation, and even console root login becomes the only recovery path.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:19.437400+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.7183369612198166,
        "confidence": 0.9998429624674172,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "214c59a178ef664b6c20bd76bda001473723cd9034aeab6b53b32c125932d9bb",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n- Step 0 (always): `sudo passwd -S <user>` (or `sudo grep <user>: /etc/shadow | cut -d: -f2`) \u2014 if it shows `L` / `*` / empty hash, no password is set.\n- If no password: ask the operator before deploy, *\"do you want me to set a password first (so non-allowlist commands prompt + work) or accept that the allowlist is a hard wall?\"*. Do not assume.\n- Even when a password exists, double-check the operator can recover via console \u2014 every Cmnd_Alias deploy needs a documented break-glass path that's been tested.\n- Keep the pre-deploy file backup at a path the new sudoers still permits to read (so post-deploy rollback to the prior policy is possible from the same shell). The 2026-05-05 deploy left the backup at `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment.bak.<TS>` \u2014 DENIED to read by the new",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:19.447702+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6555656585434472,
        "confidence": 0.9978334586352453,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "9c620896596e300a7d15f7d0fa88383421d7475d57437b5d89fd251092433b84",
        "text": "**Why:** 2026-05-05 redteam fix session. Saw `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment: sentiment ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL` and assumed \"NOPASSWD\" implied \"no password set\". Deployed Cmnd_Alias lockdown. User immediately hit `[sudo] password for sentiment:` prompts when running outside the allowlist (e.g., `tee /etc/contabo/credentials.env`, `docker compose up -d` for a config refresh). The password actually *was* set, but the user couldn't remember it \u2014 equivalent to no fallback. Recovery options collapsed to (a) Contabo VNC console root login (operator did not have access at that moment) or (b) a destructive snapshot revert (the 2026-05-05 attempt got 400/404 from the Contabo API depending on body shape \u2014 `{}` body returns 404 'Cannot POST', empty body returns 400 'body cannot be empty'). The session",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:19.445146+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6403689575305274,
        "confidence": 0.9959160938943287,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "8146703dfcd38c6c1fd3e38ca2da4c397dcaa57292dfbeba7b7c310bfdcc0800",
        "text": "**Rule:** On VPS (`sentiment@100.91.148.25`), the `sentiment` user **cannot read `.env`** and has a tightly allowlisted sudo. Treat the hardened workflow as mandatory.\n\n**Why:** Big security hardening done 2026-05-10/12. `.env` is now `root:sentiment-secrets 0640`; `sentiment` is NOT in `sentiment-secrets` (only `ftmo`, `chartapi`, `fundr` are). Sudo went from `ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL` \u2192 aliased allowlist in `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment` (`SENTIMENT_SYSTEMCTL/JOURNAL/HEALTHCHECK_WRITE/READ_CONFIG/NETDIAG/AUDIT/DOCKER/PSQL`). Previous workflow muscle memory (`sudo systemctl restart anything`, `cat .env`, `sudo psql`, `daemon-reload`) is broken by design and must not be reintroduced.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_hardened_vps2_secrets_2026-05-12.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:21.534223+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5540552304403555,
        "confidence": 0.8682022433108356,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "312b1e780623cd987a23208d96f3450e5a4379924bdf3c9aaa6a095bb5ccfeb2",
        "text": "`scripts/deploy.sh` does `${SUDO}mkdir -p '$BACKUP_DIR'` (line ~132) and `${SUDO}mkdir -p '$REMOTE_ROOT/$pdir' && ${SUDO}chown ...` (line ~144). On VPS2 with the sentiment user the sudo NOPASSWD allowlist (per `reference_vps2_sudo_allowlist.md`) covers systemctl/journalctl/PG/docker monitoring but **not `mkdir`** or `chown`. Result: deploy aborts with `sudo: a password is required` whenever the target subtree doesn't already exist on VPS2 (new research dir, new module).\n\n**Why:** Allowlist was narrowed in 2026-05-04 hardening pass; deploy.sh was written assuming broader sudo. Verified 2026-05-05 deploying EU phase 0 research files \u2014 failed on `mkdir -p /opt/backups/...` and `mkdir -p /opt/sentiment_agent/research/eu_phase0/`.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_deploy_sh_sudo_mkdir_gap.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:20.612985+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.535438998477491,
        "confidence": 0.7514263921044187,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "d86816edf5e1dc76af6b3a8d3455a3da4177c423263efb4e44b582c4d638dcd4",
        "text": "backup at `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment.bak.<TS>` \u2014 DENIED to read by the new `cat /etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment` allow-pattern (only the exact filename is whitelisted), so even reading the backup required root.\n- Pair sudoers tightening with a snapshot taken *and tested for revert* (Contabo `revert` endpoint requires the right body shape \u2014 empty `{}` returns 400, omitted body works for at least some snapshot states; verify before relying on it).\n\nAvoid the original mistake: never deploy a hard sudo lockdown without first confirming both (a) password fallback exists and (b) console recovery is reachable.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:19.455417+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6391986799001304,
        "confidence": 0.9957120250842878,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "a861b515d434b99f856d2b55cbb246dc2effd35d98652ccedac162c32f34239c",
        "text": "alerting in the same commit).\n- Live VPS3 `/etc/sudoers.d/` diverges from repo `security/sudoers.d/`: the box uses tight **per-unit** `systemctl restart <exact-unit>` grants (`91-copytrade-watchdog`, now `91-shadow-maker-recorder-watchdog`), NOT the repo's staged broad `restart *`. Mirror the per-unit pattern; never deploy the broad file.\n\nRelated: [[feedback-verify-collector-terminal-table-2026-07-14]] (phantom-gate / verify the terminal table) \u00b7 [[project_fast_maker_m1_speed_test_2026-07-09]] (engine_ws spine).\n\n---\n\n**ROOT CAUSE FOUND & FIXED (2026-07-15, master 810bb51e) \u2014 the watchdog was the safety net; THIS is the real bug.**",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/incident-shadow-maker-recorder-watchdog-autorestart-2026-07-15.md",
        "ordinal": 5,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:27.525452+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5648397375595494,
        "confidence": 0.9118463907977279,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "4fa3aa67f6b37385eaa9b43554c53eaaa7beefb5c89bf322966b84460bbe5637",
        "text": "## NON coperti (richiedono password sudo, NON eseguire autonomamente)\n\n- `apt`, `apt-get`, `apt install|update|upgrade|autoremove|clean` \u2014 install/cleanup pacchetti\n- `tee` verso path arbitrari (es. `/etc/sysctl.d/`, `/etc/logrotate.d/`) \u2014 solo `/etc/sentiment/healthcheck.url` \u00e8 coperto\n- `sysctl --system`, `sysctl -w` \u2014 tweak kernel\n- `tuned-adm profile *` \u2014 performance tuning\n- `logrotate` (esecuzione + config write)\n- `usermod`, `gpasswd`, `passwd root` \u2014 esplicitamente `!` (negate, mai concessi)\n- `visudo` \u2014 esplicitamente `!` negate\n- `cat /root/age/*` e variants \u2014 esplicitamente `!` (age key protection)\n- `docker` per container fuori dal set monitoring (no general `docker exec`, `docker run`, `docker build`)\n\n## Implicazioni operative",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference_vps2_sudo_allowlist.md",
        "ordinal": 3,

        "valid_from": null,

        "cosine": 0.5469156666670941,
        "confidence": 0.83011317511283,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"

Without one, sudo for any non-allowlisted command silently fails with \"a terminal is required to read the password\" \u2014 the operator is locked out of every ad-hoc admin operation, and even console root login becomes the only recovery path.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",

      {
        "chunk_id": "214c59a178ef664b6c20bd76bda001473723cd9034aeab6b53b32c125932d9bb",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n- Step 0 (always): `sudo passwd -S <user>` (or `sudo grep <user>: /etc/shadow | cut -d: -f2`) \u2014 if it shows `L` / `*` / empty hash, no password is set.\n- If no password: ask the operator before deploy, *\"do you want me to set a password first (so non-allowlist commands prompt + work) or accept that the allowlist is a hard wall?\"*. Do not assume.\n- Even when a password exists, double-check the operator can recover via console \u2014 every Cmnd_Alias deploy needs a documented break-glass path that's been tested.\n- Keep the pre-deploy file backup at a path the new sudoers still permits to read (so post-deploy rollback to the prior policy is possible from the same shell). The 2026-05-05 deploy left the backup at `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment.bak.<TS>` \u2014 DENIED to read by the new",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",

        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6555656585434472,
        "confidence": 0.9978334586352453,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "9c620896596e300a7d15f7d0fa88383421d7475d57437b5d89fd251092433b84",
        "text": "**Why:** 2026-05-05 redteam fix session. Saw `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment: sentiment ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL` and assumed \"NOPASSWD\" implied \"no password set\". Deployed Cmnd_Alias lockdown. User immediately hit `[sudo] password for sentiment:` prompts when running outside the allowlist (e.g., `tee /etc/contabo/credentials.env`, `docker compose up -d` for a config refresh). The password actually *was* set, but the user couldn't remember it \u2014 equivalent to no fallback. Recovery options collapsed to (a) Contabo VNC console root login (operator did not have access at that moment) or (b) a destructive snapshot revert (the 2026-05-05 attempt got 400/404 from the Contabo API depending on body shape \u2014 `{}` body returns 404 'Cannot POST', empty body returns 400 'body cannot be empty'). The session",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:19.445146+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6403689575305274,
        "confidence": 0.9959160938943287,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "8146703dfcd38c6c1fd3e38ca2da4c397dcaa57292dfbeba7b7c310bfdcc0800",
        "text": "**Rule:** On VPS (`sentiment@100.91.148.25`), the `sentiment` user **cannot read `.env`** and has a tightly allowlisted sudo. Treat the hardened workflow as mandatory.\n\n**Why:** Big security hardening done 2026-05-10/12. `.env` is now `root:sentiment-secrets 0640`; `sentiment` is NOT in `sentiment-secrets` (only `ftmo`, `chartapi`, `fundr` are). Sudo went from `ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL` \u2192 aliased allowlist in `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment` (`SENTIMENT_SYSTEMCTL/JOURNAL/HEALTHCHECK_WRITE/READ_CONFIG/NETDIAG/AUDIT/DOCKER/PSQL`). Previous workflow muscle memory (`sudo systemctl restart anything`, `cat .env`, `sudo psql`, `daemon-reload`) is broken by design and must not be reintroduced.",

        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:21.534223+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5540552304403555,
        "confidence": 0.8682022433108356,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "312b1e780623cd987a23208d96f3450e5a4379924bdf3c9aaa6a095bb5ccfeb2",
        "text": "`scripts/deploy.sh` does `${SUDO}mkdir -p '$BACKUP_DIR'` (line ~132) and `${SUDO}mkdir -p '$REMOTE_ROOT/$pdir' && ${SUDO}chown ...` (line ~144). On VPS2 with the sentiment user the sudo NOPASSWD allowlist (per `reference_vps2_sudo_allowlist.md`) covers systemctl/journalctl/PG/docker monitoring but **not `mkdir`** or `chown`. Result: deploy aborts with `sudo: a password is required` whenever the target subtree doesn't already exist on VPS2 (new research dir, new module).\n\n**Why:** Allowlist was narrowed in 2026-05-04 hardening pass; deploy.sh was written assuming broader sudo. Verified 2026-05-05 deploying EU phase 0 research files \u2014 failed on `mkdir -p /opt/backups/...` and `mkdir -p /opt/sentiment_agent/research/eu_phase0/`.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_deploy_sh_sudo_mkdir_gap.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:20.612985+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.535438998477491,
        "confidence": 0.7514263921044187,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "d86816edf5e1dc76af6b3a8d3455a3da4177c423263efb4e44b582c4d638dcd4",
        "text": "backup at `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment.bak.<TS>` \u2014 DENIED to read by the new `cat /etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment` allow-pattern (only the exact filename is whitelisted), so even reading the backup required root.\n- Pair sudoers tightening with a snapshot taken *and tested for revert* (Contabo `revert` endpoint requires the right body shape \u2014 empty `{}` returns 400, omitted body works for at least some snapshot states; verify before relying on it).\n\nAvoid the original mistake: never deploy a hard sudo lockdown without first confirming both (a) password fallback exists and (b) console recovery is reachable.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:19.455417+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6391986799001304,
        "confidence": 0.9957120250842878,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "a861b515d434b99f856d2b55cbb246dc2effd35d98652ccedac162c32f34239c",
        "text": "alerting in the same commit).\n- Live VPS3 `/etc/sudoers.d/` diverges from repo `security/sudoers.d/`: the box uses tight **per-unit** `systemctl restart <exact-unit>` grants (`91-copytrade-watchdog`, now `91-shadow-maker-recorder-watchdog`), NOT the repo's staged broad `restart *`. Mirror the per-unit pattern; never deploy the broad file.\n\nRelated: [[feedback-verify-collector-terminal-table-2026-07-14]] (phantom-gate / verify the terminal table) \u00b7 [[project_fast_maker_m1_speed_test_2026-07-09]] (engine_ws spine).\n\n---\n\n**ROOT CAUSE FOUND & FIXED (2026-07-15, master 810bb51e) \u2014 the watchdog was the safety net; THIS is the real bug.**",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/incident-shadow-maker-recorder-watchdog-autorestart-2026-07-15.md",
        "ordinal": 5,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:27.525452+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5648397375595494,
        "confidence": 0.9118463907977279,
        "verdict": "ok",
        "authority": "unknown"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "4fa3aa67f6b37385eaa9b43554c53eaaa7beefb5c89bf322966b84460bbe5637",
        "text": "## NON coperti (richiedono password sudo, NON eseguire autonomamente)\n\n- `apt`, `apt-get`, `apt install|update|upgrade|autoremove|clean` \u2014 install/cleanup pacchetti\n- `tee` verso path arbitrari (es. `/etc/sysctl.d/`, `/etc/logrotate.d/`) \u2014 solo `/etc/sentiment/healthcheck.url` \u00e8 coperto\n- `sysctl --system`, `sysctl -w` \u2014 tweak kernel\n- `tuned-adm profile *` \u2014 performance tuning\n- `logrotate` (esecuzione + config write)\n- `usermod`, `gpasswd`, `passwd root` \u2014 esplicitamente `!` (negate, mai concessi)\n- `visudo` \u2014 esplicitamente `!` negate\n- `cat /root/age/*` e variants \u2014 esplicitamente `!` (age key protection)\n- `docker` per container fuori dal set monitoring (no general `docker exec`, `docker run`, `docker build`)\n\n## Implicazioni operative",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/reference_vps2_sudo_allowlist.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:06:27.902162+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,

        "cosine": 0.5469156666670941,
        "confidence": 0.83011317511283,

        "text": "Before deploying any sudoers lockdown that replaces wildcard `NOPASSWD: ALL` with a Cmnd_Alias allowlist, **verify whether the target user has a password set**. Without one, sudo for any non-allowlisted command silently fails with \"a terminal is required to read the password\" \u2014 the operator is locked out of every ad-hoc admin operation, and even console root login becomes the only recovery path.",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:19.437400+00:00",

        "verdict": "ok",

      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "214c59a178ef664b6c20bd76bda001473723cd9034aeab6b53b32c125932d9bb",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n- Step 0 (always): `sudo passwd -S <user>` (or `sudo grep <user>: /etc/shadow | cut -d: -f2`) \u2014 if it shows `L` / `*` / empty hash, no password is set.\n- If no password: ask the operator before deploy, *\"do you want me to set a password first (so non-allowlist commands prompt + work) or accept that the allowlist is a hard wall?\"*. Do not assume.\n- Even when a password exists, double-check the operator can recover via console \u2014 every Cmnd_Alias deploy needs a documented break-glass path that's been tested.\n- Keep the pre-deploy file backup at a path the new sudoers still permits to read (so post-deploy rollback to the prior policy is possible from the same shell). The 2026-05-05 deploy left the backup at `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment.bak.<TS>` \u2014 DENIED to read by the new",
        "source": "sentiment-agent/feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-09-13T08:05:19.447702+00:00",
